A 63-year-old man with hypertension and insulin-treated type 2 diabetes presented with orthostatic dizziness and presyncope. Antihypertensive therapy was intensified for elevated seated BP. After intensification, upright tolerance worsened, with recurrent syncope, a rib fracture, and loss of functional independence. Symptoms remained disabling despite antihypertensive withdrawal and nonpharmacological measures. Supine-to-seated-to-standing assessment showed a BP fall from 197/99 mm Hg supine to 122/81 mm Hg seated and 79/56 mm Hg standing, with presyncope and heart rate increasing from 72 to 86 beats/min. Supine measurements and 24-hour BP monitoring documented severe supine and nocturnal hypertension, reverse dipping, and mean asleep BP 203/107 mm Hg. Autonomic testing demonstrated combined cardiovagal and adrenergic dysfunction, supporting neurogenic orthostatic hypotension due to diabetic autonomic neuropathy. Management was tailored to upright and recumbent periods. A removable transdermal nitroglycerin patch was used overnight. Nonpharmacological measures included repeated encouragement to increase fluid intake, but daily intake generally remained below 2 L. Clinical assessment suggested relative volume depletion. Low-dose morning fludrocortisone was introduced cautiously despite severe supine/nocturnal hypertension. After upright tolerance improved, morning lercanidipine was added. Subsequent 24-hour BP monitoring showed a more balanced profile. Orthostatic symptoms and upright tolerance improved. No further syncope or falls occurred, and functional independence improved. Later 24-hour BP monitoring showed reduced nocturnal predominance, with mean awake/asleep BP 164/86 and 165/89 mm Hg, respectively. Mild peripheral edema was managed with intermittent torasemide. This case illustrates how integrating postural BP responses with 24-hour BP patterns can identify competing hemodynamic phenotypes that may require different management during upright and recumbent periods. Repeated reassessment and individualized treatment adaptation according to the documented BP pattern and clinical context may help balance competing risks of upright hypoperfusion and supine/nocturnal hypertension.

title: Electrocardiographic markers of arrhythmic risk after renal sympathetic denervation in resistant hypertension.
text: Renal sympathetic denervation (RDN) has emerged as a device-based therapy for resistant hypertension; however, its effects on electrocardiographic (ECG) markers related to arrhythmic risk remain incompletely defined. We aimed to evaluate changes in ECG indices reflecting atrial and ventricular electrical heterogeneity in patients undergoing RDN compared to medically treated controls. This retrospective cohort study included 263 patients with resistant hypertension (RDN+, n = 120; RDN-, n = 143) with baseline and 6-month ECG recordings. ECG parameters included the P-wave dispersion, Tp-Te interval, and frontal QRS-T angle. To account for baseline differences, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPW) based on propensity scores was applied. Weighted linear regression models with doubly robust adjustment were used to estimate the independent association between RDN and follow-up ECG parameters after adjusting for baseline ECG values and change in SBP. At 6 months, patients undergoing RDN demonstrated significantly lower P-wave dispersion (27.4 vs. 37.5 ms, P < 0.001), Tp-Te interval (80.3 vs. 84.7 ms, P = 0.028), and frontal QRS-T angle (26 vs. 37°, P = 0.026) compared with controls. In the weighted models, RDN remained independently associated with reductions in these parameters. In patients with resistant hypertension, renal sympathetic denervation was associated with improvements in ECG markers related to arrhythmic risk at 6 months, which were not fully explained by changes in office SBP.

title: Evaluation of a population health strategy to improve albuminuria detection among primary care patients with hypertension.
text: To study the impact of an electronic health record (EHR) alert implemented in September 2022 that prompts annual orders for urine albumin-creatinine ratio (UACR) testing for adults with hypertension (HTN). Using segmented interrupted time-series analyses and comparative interrupted time-series analyses stratified by diabetes status, we evaluated changes in annual UACR testing rates among adults with hypertension from 1 January 2021 through 30 June 2025. Among 26 048 hypertensive adults (mean age, 61 years; 38.5% with diabetes), annual UACR testing rates increased from 23.8% preintervention to 37.1% postintervention. Implementation was associated with an immediate 4.05-fold increase in the odds of monthly UACR testing [odds ratio (OR) 4.05, 95% confidence interval (CI) 3.84-4.28]. Patients without diabetes experienced a larger immediate increase than patients with diabetes (OR 2.62, 95% CI 2.45-2.80). Patients with UACR at least 30 mg/g were more likely to receive angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor/angiotensin receptor blockers and SGLT2 inhibitor therapy than patients with UACR less than 30 mg/g or those never tested (P < 0.001). Implementation of an EHR-integrated UACR alert increased annual UACR testing among adults with HTN. Irrespective of the EHR alert, UACR testing was associated with greater use of guideline-concordant medications. This easily implemented intervention has the potential to improve guideline-concordant care for patients with HTN in primary care.

title: Completeness of care provision and inequalities in care for people with hypertension, diabetes, and obesity: an analysis of the Brazilian National Basic Health Units Census.
text: This study aimed to identify patterns and inequalities in the completeness of care provision for people with hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and obesity in Brazilian primary health care (PHC), drawing on the 2024 Brazilian National Basic Health Units Census (BHU Census). This was a cross-sectional online survey covering 44,938 BHUs registered in the Brazilian National Registry of Health Establishments and validated by municipal health managers. Variables related to geographic region, municipal characteristics, and health service characteristics were analyzed. Care provision was considered complete when the response was positive for all 14 actions related to hypertension, 15 for diabetes, and 10 for obesity. A low proportion of BHUs demonstrated complete provision of care for people with hypertension (15.3%), diabetes (15.6%), and obesity (13.4%), across all regions and municipality profiles. Completeness was higher in the Southeast and Northeast and lower in the South. Large municipalities, municipalities with high or very high social vulnerability, and municipalities with 100% family health coverage also showed higher completeness levels. After adjusting for contextual and BHU characteristics, the family health was associated with 70% higher completeness of care provision. Although access to consultations is well established, weaknesses persist in comprehensiveness and care coordination for chronic diseases, highlighting the need for structural policies that strengthen the capacity of PHC to effectively address health needs. El estudio tuvo como objetivo establecer patrones y desigualdades en la completitud de la oferta de acciones dirigidas a personas con hipertensión arterial sistémica, diabetes mellitus tipo 2 y obesidad en la atención primaria de salud (APS) brasileña, basándose en el Censo Nacional de las Unidades Básicas de Salud (Censo de las UBS), realizado en 2024. Se trata de una encuesta en línea, que abarcó 44.938 UBS registradas en el Catastro Nacional de Establecimientos de Salud y validadas por los gestores municipales. Se analizaron las variables relacionadas con la región geopolítica, el perfil de los municipios y los servicios de salud. Se consideró completa la oferta de atención cuando la respuesta fue positiva para las 14 acciones relacionadas con la hipertensión, las 15 con la diabetes y las 10 con la obesidad. Se observó una baja proporción de UBS con completitud de la oferta de atención a personas con hipertensión (15,3%), diabetes (15,6%) y obesidad (13,4%), en todas las regiones y perfiles de municipio. La completitud de la oferta fue mayor en las regiones Sudeste y Nordeste, y menor en el Sur. Los grandes municipios, así como aquellos con una vulnerabilidad social muy alta y con una cobertura municipal de salud de la familia del 100%, también demostraron una mayor completitud. Tras ajustar por características contextuales y de las UBS, el modelo salud de la familia aumentó en un 70% la completitud de la oferta. Aunque el acceso a consultas está consolidado, siguen existiendo debilidades en la integralidad y en la coordinación de la atención de enfermedades crónicas, lo que exige políticas estructurales que fortalezcan la capacidad resolutiva de la APS.

title: Clinical Protocols and Guidelines for Hypertension and Diabetes in Incarcerated Populations: A Scoping Review.
text: Incarcerated populations have a disproportionate burden of acute and chronic conditions, including hypertension and diabetes. We aimed to identify and describe clinical protocols and guidelines for managing hypertension and diabetes in the incarcerated population. We conducted a scoping review in July 2025 of clinical protocols and guidelines that address the prevention, promotion, screening, diagnosis, and treatment of hypertension and diabetes in the incarcerated population. We searched electronic databases (Medline/PubMed, Embase, the Virtual Health Library, EBSCOhost, Scopus, Cochrane, and Web of Science), gray literature repositories, and websites of governmental and international organizations. We used the AGREE II instrument to assess document quality. Three documents met the inclusion criteria; they were published in 2021, 2022, and 2024 and originated from high-income countries. Methodological appraisal showed heterogeneity in guideline development, with consistently low scores in the domains of stakeholder involvement and rigor of development. Existing protocols encompass health education and self-management support, multidisciplinary care, universal screening at intake, evidence-based and individualized treatment, and intersectoral collaboration to ensure health care delivery in correctional settings. The small number of clinical protocols addressing hypertension and diabetes management in the incarcerated population reflects a critical normative gap in correctional health systems. Strengthening the scientific rigor of these protocols and ensuring their implementation are essential to standardize care, reduce clinical variation, and promote health equity, both within correctional settings and in the transition back to the community.

title: Challenges in accessing health information among patients with uncontrolled hypertension in Singapore: a qualitative study.
text: Accessing health information is the crucial first step before an individual can understand, appraise, and apply it to improve their health. Health information is important for patients with chronic diseases such as hypertension, where effective self-management is essential for disease control. This is particularly critical for patients with uncontrolled hypertension, who are at higher risk of life-threatening complications. Thus, this study aimed to explore the gaps in accessing health information among patients with uncontrolled hypertension. A descriptive-interpretative qualitative research was conducted in 2024 at three public primary care clinics. Patients with uncontrolled hypertension were recruited through purposive sampling. Individual in-depth interviews were done by trained researchers in participants' preferred language, using a semi-structured interview guide. The interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim. The transcripts were managed using NVivo 14 and analysed thematically using an inductive approach. A total of 17 patients (age 46 to 80 years old; 52.9% male; 70.6% Chinese) were interviewed. The patients in this study often accessed health information on hypertension management from two main sources: primary care providers (PCPs) providers and online platforms. The challenges they experienced with accessing health information included: generic advice from PCPs and uncertainty about online credibility, insufficient information from PCPs and overwhelming online information, inconsistent health information, and prioritisation of health information on diabetes over hypertension. This study highlights the challenges in accessing personalised, trustworthy, consistent and actionable health information among patients with uncontrolled hypertension. These challenges underscore their lack of ability to appraise and subsequently use health information appropriately. This study also reveals significant gaps both in the provision of health information by PCPs and patients' ability to evaluate online information.

title: Prevalence, associations and sex-related disparities of hypertension in South Asians: Evidence from a national survey of Sri Lanka.
text: Blood pressure(BP) control remains suboptimal worldwide. Sex-related disparities in hypertension have been reported, but data from South Asia are limited. Understanding the epidemiology and sex-related differences is essential to improve BP control. To assess the prevalence, associations and sex-related disparities of hypertension among Sri Lankans. We analysed secondary data from the Sri Lanka STEPS Survey 2021, a nationally representative, community-based, cross-sectional study. Hypertension was defined as BP ≥ 140/90 mmHg or current antihypertensive use; controlled BP as BP < 140/90 mmHg. Prevalences, associations, and sex-related disparities in hypertension, undiagnosed hypertension, and BP control were assessed using logistic regression. Data from 4,634 adults(mean age 43.5(weighted CI 43.0-44.1) years; female 54.8 (53.1-56.5)%) were analysed. Overall, 37.2(35.5-38.9)% had hypertension, of whom 60.0(58.1-63.4) % were previously undiagnosed. Among those previously diagnosed, 73.6 (73.6, 69.6-77.2)% were on treatment, but only 38.0(33.0-44.20)% achieved BP targets. The rates of hypertension prevalence (p = 0.600), treated hypertension (p = 0.398), and controlled blood pressure (p = 0.819) in females and males did not differ significantly by sex. However, undiagnosed hypertension was significantly higher in males (69.4%, 65.3-73.1) than in females (53.6%, 50.1-57.0) (p < 0.001). Differences in the associations of hypertension by sex were noted; diabetes was associated only in females (p < 0.001), while wealth quintile (p < 0.001) and 24-hour urinary salt excretion (p = 0.011) were associated only in males. Overweight/obesity was shown to have a significant association with undiagnosed hypertension only in males (p = 0.017) in stratified analyses. More than half of the hypertensives in this South Asian population were previously undiagnosed. Of hypertensives, ¾ were treated, but only 1/3 achieved treatment goals. Prevalence, treatment and control rates of hypertension were not different between females and males, but undiagnosed hypertension was more common in men. Therefore, the emphasis should be on improving the detection of hypertension, especially in men, and on treating to targets in both sexes.

title: Dapagliflozin attenuates progression from prefrailty to frailty in patients with hypertension and chronic kidney disease.
text: BACKGROUNDChronic kidney disease (CKD) and hypertension share common pathophysiological pathways contributing to vascular damage, endothelial dysfunction, and physical decline, particularly in older adults with prefrailty. To evaluate the relationship among renal injury, physical performance, and frailty progression in hypertensive older adults with CKD and assess whether dapagliflozin associates with reduced frailty progression, we designed the study DAPA-FORTRESS (DAPAgliflozin and Frailty prOgression in hypeRTension and chRonic kidnEy diSeaSe).METHODSWe enrolled 135 prefrail hypertensive patients with CKD aged >65 years and followed them for 1 year. After coarsened exact matching, our balanced cohort had 105 patients (52 dapagliflozin). Associations between albuminuria, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and physical performance were analyzed using correlation and regression models. Effect of dapagliflozin on frailty progression was evaluated using multivariable logistic regression.RESULTSA significant inverse association between gait speed and albuminuria (r2 = 0.48, P < 0.0001) and significant positive linear association between gait speed and eGFR (r2 = 0.18; P < 0.0001) were observed. Patients with eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 exhibited significantly worse physical performance than those with higher eGFR (P = 0.0003). In adjusted analyses, receiving dapagliflozin was independently associated with lower odds of progressing to frailty at 1 year (OR = 0.130; CI 0.045-0.381; P < 0.001).CONCLUSIONIn older hypertensive patients with CKD, greater renal injury is associated with worse physical performance, while dapagliflozin use reduces the risk of frailty progression. These findings indicate a potential protective role of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibition in mitigating functional decline in this high-risk population.FUNDINGNIH: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (R01-HL146691), National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (R01-DK123259); American Heart Association (AHA- 24IPA1268813, AHA-22-915561, AHA-24-1195524).

title: Rationale and Design of a Parallel Randomized Trial of a DASH-Enhanced Portfolio Diet With or Without Ultra-Processed Plant Proteins for Blood Pressure and Other Cardiometabolic Risk Factors in Adults With Hypertension and Obesity: The Substitution of High With Low Ultra-Processed Soy Protein Foods in a Guideline-Based Diet Intervention on Cardiometabolic Health Trial.
text: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death and hospitalization globally. Clinical practice guidelines recommend various plant-based dietary patterns that target specific cardiometabolic risk factors, including the Dietary Approach to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet for blood pressure and the Portfolio diet for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Combining key elements of these patterns may enhance cardiovascular disease risk reduction. However, many soy-based products, a key Portfolio component, are classified as ultra-processed foods (UPFs). This trial will answer 2 questions: (1) Does a DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet result in clinically meaningful reductions in blood pressure compared with standard of care and (2) Is a high-UPF noninferior to a low-UPF soy protein-containing DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet for blood pressure reduction? The SWITCH (Substitution of High With Low Ultra-Processed Soy Protein Foods in a Guideline-Based Diet Intervention for Cardiometabolic Health) trial is a parallel, randomized, 3-arm, open-label, superiority-noninferiority trial. Three hundred adults with hypertension and obesity, including 50% with type 2 diabetes, will be randomized to a high-UPF or low-UPF soy protein-containing DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet or standard of care for 12 weeks. The primary outcome is systolic blood pressure. Key secondary outcomes are non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol and body weight. Other outcomes include cardiometabolic risk factors. Findings will provide high-quality evidence on the use of a DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet and the role of nutrient-dense soy foods classified as UPFs within the combination of the 2 guideline-based dietary patterns to support dietary strategies for cardiometabolic risk reduction. URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/; Unique identifier: NCT06907862.
source: Journal of the American Heart Association

title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors in World Health Organization Group 1 Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: A REVEAL Lite 2-Matched Cohort With Time-Varying Exposure Analysis.
text: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) improve outcomes across several cardiometabolic conditions, but their role in World Health Organization group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains uncertain. We conducted a retrospective, single-center cohort study of adults with group 1 PAH. Patients prescribed SGLT2i were compared with patients without exposure. Propensity-score matching was performed 1:2 using age, sex, baseline REVEAL Lite 2 risk category, diabetes mellitus, and statin use. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality, and the secondary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events. Associations were evaluated using fixed-exposure and start-stop time-varying Cox models. The matched cohort included 366 patients: 122 (33%) receiving SGLT2i and 244 (67%) controls. Most patients were classified as high risk by REVEAL Lite 2 (106 SGLT2i recipients (87%) and 215 controls (88%), respectively). In the fixed-exposure analysis, SGLT2i use was associated with lower mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.53; 95% CI, 0.31-0.91; P=.018), without a significant difference in major adverse cardiovascular events (HR, 1.23; 95% CI, 0.93-1.63; P=.14). In the time-varying analysis, SGLT2i exposure was not significantly associated with mortality (HR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.26-2.11; P=.57). The apparent survival association was attenuated after accounting for treatment timing, demonstrating the sensitivity of observational PAH estimates to exposure classification and supporting prospective randomized trials.
source: Mayo Clinic proceedings. Innovations, quality & outcomes

title: Long-term trends, age-period-cohort patterns, and future projections of incident stroke with comorbid hypertension and diabetes among older adults in Shenzhen, China: a population-based surveillance study.
text: Older adults with stroke frequently have coexisting hypertension and diabetes, a high-risk cardiometabolic profile that complicates prevention, long-term management, and health service planning. However, population-based evidence on the long-term incidence trajectory of stroke occurring with both conditions remains limited, particularly in rapidly urbanizing settings undergoing population ageing. This study examined long-term trends, age-period-cohort patterns, and future projections of incident stroke with comorbid hypertension and diabetes among older adults in Shenzhen, China. This population-based retrospective surveillance study used data from the Shenzhen Cardiovascular and Cerebrovascular Disease Registry System. Incident stroke events registered between 1 January 2004 and 31 December 2023 among adults aged ≥ 60 years were identified, and 40,128 events with comorbid hypertension and diabetes were included. Crude incidence rates (CIRs) and age-standardized incidence rates (ASIRs) were calculated. Joinpoint regression, age-period-cohort analysis, and Bayesian age-period-cohort modeling were used to assess temporal trends, estimate age, period, and cohort effects, and project incidence trends from 2024 to 2033. From 2004 to 2023, the number of incident stroke events with comorbid hypertension and diabetes increased from 314 to 3,336, and the ASIR rose from 141.12 per 100,000 in 2004 to 414.78 per 100,000 in 2023. Joinpoint regression showed overall increasing trends in CIR and ASIR across the study period, with average annual percent changes of 5.44% and 6.14%, respectively, while identifying a late-period decline after 2017. Incidence levels were generally higher in males than in females. Age-period-cohort analysis showed marked age effects, elevated period-related risks in recent periods, and increasing cohort effects across successive birth cohorts. Bayesian projections suggested that both CIR and ASIR may increase from 2024 to 2033, with larger projected increases in males. Among older adults in Shenzhen, the burden of stroke with comorbid hypertension and diabetes showed a long-term upward trajectory over the study period. Model-based projections suggested that the burden may increase from 2024 to 2033, particularly among males and older age groups. These findings provide population-level descriptive and projection evidence that may inform risk stratification and health service planning for ageing urban populations.

title: Development and Validation of a Prediction Model for Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension in Diabetic Patients: A Retrospective Study of 57,375 Patients.
text: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is an important cardiopulmonary complication in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), yet practical models integrating routinely available clinical, laboratory, and echocardiographic information remain limited. We conducted a single-center retrospective electronic medical record cohort study with a prespecified temporal split. Patients admitted from January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2021 formed the training cohort, and those admitted from January 1, 2022 to July 31, 2025 formed the temporal validation cohort. Among 47,042 pre-2022 records screened, 10,458 eligible patients were included in the training cohort, including 423 patients with PAH (4.0%); among 60,069 later records screened, 14,060 patients were included in the validation cohort, including 600 patients with PAH (4.3%). Nine prespecified clinical domains were initially evaluated. Because tricuspid regurgitation velocity/gradient contributed to the echocardiographic PAH classification, a sensitivity analysis excluded the PAH-related pressure-gradient domain from the exploratory combined model to reduce incorporation bias. In the training-cohort sensitivity analysis, cardiac cavity and vascular dilatation was the strongest remaining individual discriminator (area under the curve [AUC], 0.819), followed by coagulation dysfunction (AUC, 0.697) and cardiac dysfunction (AUC, 0.627); the pressure-gradient-excluded combined model achieved an AUC of 0.823. When applied without refitting to the temporal validation cohort, this sensitivity model achieved an AUC of 0.780. The eight-variable echocardiography-informed nomogram had a C-index of 0.666 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.631-0.699), with a Hosmer-Lemeshow p value of 0.453. Because the nomogram includes echocardiographic predictors, including tricuspid regurgitation velocity and pulmonary valve velocity, it is intended for risk stratification after echocardiography rather than pre-echocardiographic screening or prediction of incident PAH. Diabetes-specific variables such as HbA1c, diabetes duration, treatment exposure, insulin resistance indices, and microvascular complications were not consistently available in the historical records and were not modeled. Prospective multicenter studies with systematic collection of diabetes-specific variables are needed.

title: Reduced Risk of MASLD and Cardiometabolic Disease Following Renal Denervation Therapy in Patients With Resistant Hypertension.
text: Autonomic dysfunction increases the risk of cardio-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), type 2 diabetes (T2D), cardiovascular disease (CVD) and chronic kidney disease (CKD). Renal denervation reduces renal sympathetic nerve activity and lowers blood pressure independent of long-term pharmacotherapy, with potential downstream effects on metabolic and hepatic pathways. We aimed to evaluate the impact of renal denervation, compared with intensive antihypertensive therapy, on cardiometabolic disease risk. We conducted a target trial emulation using the TriNetX global federated health research network. Eligible participants were adults with hypertension (ICD-10 code I10) who were treated with either renal denervation therapy and pharmacological treatment (identified via ICD-10 or Current Procedural Terminology codes), acting as the treatment group, or an intensive pharmacological antihypertensive regime (four of a beta blocker, calcium channel blocker, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor, angiotensin II receptor blocker, alpha blocker or diuretic), acting as the control group. Propensity score matching (1:1) balanced the treatment and control groups, accounting for confounding variables. The primary outcome was of MASLD/metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), while secondary outcomes included T2D, CKD and a composite of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE): sudden cardiac death, ischaemic heart disease (IHD), cerebrovascular accident (CVA), peripheral vascular disease (PVD) and heart failure (HF). Cox regression generated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). After matching, 1735 patients remained in each group, with well-balanced baseline characteristics (mean age 42 vs. 41 years; standardised mean difference [SMD] 0.05; 52.6% vs. 54.3% male; SMD 0.03). After PSM, renal denervation was associated with a lower risk of MASLD (HR 0.38 [0.29, 0.51]), T2D (HR 0.21 [0.13, 0.33]), CKD (HR 0.26 [0.20, 0.35]), MACE (HR 0.46 [0.34, 0.62]), IHD (HR 0.56 [0.39, 0.80]), CVA (HR 0.33 [0.20, 0.52]) and HF (HR 0.39 [0.25, 0.62]). Control of the sympathetic nervous system with renal denervation therapy in patients with resistant hypertension is associated with a lower risk of incident CKM syndrome including MASLD, T2D, CVD and CKD, supporting the role of autonomic dysfunction in the progression of cardiometabolic disease.

title: Finerenone-Empagliflozin Combination Therapy in Apparent Resistant Hypertension: A CONFIDENCE Trial Post Hoc Analysis.
text: Apparent treatment-resistant hypertension (aTRH) is common in chronic kidney disease (CKD) with type 2 diabetes and predicts worse outcomes. Spironolactone, the established fourth-line agent, is limited by hyperkalemia in CKD. This analysis assessed whether finerenone plus empagliflozin lowers blood pressure (BP) meaningfully in aTRH, and whether aTRH modifies these agents' efficacy and safety. Post hoc analysis of CONFIDENCE (NCT05254002), a double-blind randomized trial of finerenone, empagliflozin, or both in CKD with albuminuria and type 2 diabetes. aTRH was BP ≥130/80 mm Hg on 3 antihypertensive drugs, or ≥4 drugs regardless of BP. Mixed models and logistic regression identified predictors of BP response. Of the 796 participants, 307 (39%) had aTRH; they were older, more obese, and had more atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, higher albuminuria, and higher systolic BP (140.9 vs 131.5 mm Hg) but similar estimated glomerular filtration rate (53 vs 55 mL/min/1.73 m2). Combination therapy lowered systolic BP more than either monotherapy. Independent predictors of a ≥10 mm Hg systolic BP fall were aTRH (OR: 1.56; 95% CI: 1.08-2.25) and higher baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (OR: 1.15 per 10 mL/min/1.73 m2; 95% CI: 1.05-1.26); diuretic use and albuminuria were not. The aTRH effect was treatment-independent (interaction P = 0.21). Adverse events were more frequent with aTRH (63.8% vs 51.1%), yet on combination therapy hyperkalemia was less frequent (11.2% vs 17.5%). aTRH affected approximately 40% of participants and marked a higher-risk phenotype responsive to finerenone-empagliflozin, with BP reductions comparable to spironolactone but without the excess hyperkalemia that limits its use in CKD.

title: Population-specific association and risk discrimination utility of the cardiometabolic index for prevalent hypertension-diabetes comorbidity: insights from CHARLS and NHANES.
text: The comorbidity of cardiometabolic diseases, such as hypertension and diabetes, is increasingly prevalent worldwide, particularly among middle-aged and elderly populations. The cardiometabolic index (CMI), a novel composite biomarker integrating features of dyslipidemia and abdominal obesity, has emerged as a potential indicator. However, its association with prevalent hypertension-diabetes comorbidity and its risk discrimination utility across Chinese and American populations remain insufficiently investigated. This investigation utilized data from CHARLS and NHANES, encompassing 12,261 Chinese and 1,329 American participants. Multivariable logistic regression models and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses were employed to evaluate the association and dose-response relationship between CMI and prevalent hypertension-diabetes comorbidity. Machine learning models were constructed to evaluate risk discrimination performance, including LightGBM, GBM, and CatBoost. Mediation analysis was further conducted to assess the potential mediating role of body mass index (BMI) in the association between CMI and the outcome. Elevated CMI was significantly associated with an increased risk of hypertension-diabetes comorbidity (CHARLS: OR = 2.16, 95% CI: 2.00-2.34; NHANES: OR = 1.99, 95% CI: 1.48-2.69). RCS analysis revealed a marked nonlinear association within the Chinese cohort (threshold effect, P-nonlinear < 0.001), contrasting with a more linear relationship in the American population (P-nonlinear = 0.764). Among the machine learning models, LightGBM and GBM demonstrated superior risk discrimination performance (CHARLS AUC = 0.841; NHANES AUC = 0.948). Mediation analysis indicated that BMI exerted a significant partial mediating effect, accounting for 32.90% and 43.32% of the total association in the Chinese and American cohorts, respectively. CMI was independently associated with prevalent hypertension-diabetes comorbidity, with notable population-specific differences in association patterns. Machine learning models incorporating CMI showed favorable risk discrimination performance. The partial mediation effect of BMI underscores the critical importance of adiposity management in mitigating cardiometabolic risk. This study provides a novel theoretical framework and methodological support for cross-population cardiometabolic health assessment.

title: Modified-Release Trazodone for Acute Major Depressive Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
text: Modified-release (MR) trazodone formulations (prolonged-release [PR] and once-a-day [OAD]) are used to treat acute major depressive disorder (MDD), but there has been no quantitative synthesis of the available double-blind randomized evidence. We assessed the efficacy and tolerability of MR trazodone in adults with acute MDD. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Europe PMC, and ClinicalTrials.gov up to 24 February 2026 and Scopus up to 6 March 2026. We also screened the reference lists of the identified publications for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of trazodone PR or OAD in adults with acute MDD. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed when at least 2 trials were available. Five primary RCTs (N=1329 randomized) met the inclusion criteria: 2 were placebo-controlled and 3 were active-controlled. Compared with placebo, MR trazodone improved HAM-D-17 scores (mean difference in symptom improvement: 2.49; 95% CI: 1.48-3.51) and increased the response rate (risk ratio [RR]: 1.44; 95% CI: 1.19-1.75). Remission rates were higher but imprecise (RR: 1.32; 95% CI: 0.93-1.88). Discontinuation due to adverse events occurred more frequently than with placebo (RR: 3.57; 95% CI: 1.79-7.10). In head-to-head trials, the estimates versus SSRIs were imprecise and did not demonstrate equivalence. A single venlafaxine XR trial favored venlafaxine. On the basis of 2 placebo-controlled trials, MR trazodone was found to be more effective than a placebo for reducing acute adult MDD symptoms in the short term. Sparse active-comparator evidence does not demonstrate superiority or equivalence compared with standard antidepressants. Real-world data may provide complementary information when insomnia or anxious distress is prominent.

title: Baseline cortical structural features are associated with depressive and cognitive improvement in major depressive disorder.
text: Major depressive disorder (MDD) exhibits substantial clinical and neurobiological heterogeneity, along with marked variability in treatment response, underscoring the need for objective neuroimaging markers to inform personalized interventions. Twenty-two patients with MDD and twenty-one age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HCs) were enrolled. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the 17-item Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression (HAMD17), and the Hamilton Rating Scale for Anxiety (HAMA), while cognitive function was evaluated with the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status (RBANS). Structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) was performed to assess cortical features in MDD patients and HCs. Cortical morphological features [fractal dimension (FD), gyrification index (GI), sulcus depth (SD), and cortical thickness (CT)] were quantified using the automated Computational Anatomy Toolbox (CAT12). Multiple regression analyses were conducted to identify cortical regions in which baseline morphology was associated with subsequent depressive and cognitive changes, controlling for age and sex (voxel-wise p < 0.001, family wise error corrected cluster-level p < 0.05). To further assess the stability and potential out-of-sample consistency of these associations, exploratory leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) analyses with permutation testing were performed. Baseline FD in the left superior frontal cortex (SFC), left cuneus, right rostral middle frontal cortex and right lateral occipital cortex (LOC), GI in the left LOC, and CT in the bilateral insula and pericalcarine cortex were significantly associated with greater improvement in depressive symptoms following antidepressant treatment. In addition, lower baseline SD in the left LOC was associated with greater improvement in delayed memory. Single-ROI models (adjusted for age and sex) revealed that baseline left cuneus FD and left SFC FD was significantly correlated with changes in HAMD17 and HAMA, respectively, and the baseline left LOC/lingual SD showed a moderate cross-validated correlation with delayed memory change. These associations were supported by permutation testing, whereas the model for memory improvement showed only exploratory, non-significant cross-validated performance. Baseline cortical morphometric features were associated with clinical and cognitive changes following antidepressant treatment in MDD. Single-ROI LOOCV models based on left cuneus and left SFC FD showed cross-validated associations with symptom improvement. These findings are preliminary and should be interpreted with caution, pending replication in independent cohorts.

title: The biological basis underlying the local brain functional changes of taVNS in treating major depressive disorder: An imaging transcriptomics study.
text: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is a promising non-invasive intervention for major depressive disorder (MDD). However, the molecular basis underlying functional brain changes associated with taVNS treatment remains poorly understood. In this prospective longitudinal cohort study, 122 patients with MDD were included in the final analysis from an initial sample of 172 enrolled participants, with 50 excluded owing to dropout or incomplete data. These participants underwent resting-state fMRI before and after 8 weeks of taVNS treatment. For each of the 246 Brainnetome Atlas regions, we calculated treatment-related changes in the amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (ALFF) and regional homogeneity (ReHo). These changes were correlated with symptom improvement (HAMD-17) to generate specific ALFF and ReHo response maps. To explore candidate spatial molecular associations, we linked these response maps to whole-brain gene expression profiles from the Allen Human Brain Atlas (15,633 genes) via LASSO regression with cross-validation, followed by gene-set enrichment analysis and spatial correlation with 32 PET-based neurotransmitter receptor/transporter maps. In this single-arm study, 86 participants (70.5%) met the response criterion. Given the absence of a control group, this reflects treatment-related improvement rather than direct evidence of taVNS efficacy. Imaging transcriptomics revealed that gene expression was spatially associated with both response maps, with higher cross-validated regional prediction performance for ReHo (R2 = 0.309, r = 0.558) than for ALFF (R2 = 0.174, r = 0.418). ALFF responses were spatially enriched for cation channel and NMDA receptor-related pathways, whereas ReHo responses were predominantly enriched for microglial and interferon-related immune signaling. The ReHo response map correlated most strongly with GABA-A receptor density, while ALFF changes showed closer links to κ-opioid and CB1 receptor distributions. These results indicate that the functional changes associated with taVNS treatment show spatial transcriptomic enrichment for distinct synaptic and neuroimmune pathways, providing candidate molecular correlates to guide further study of this neuromodulation approach in MDD.

title: A novel theta-frequency tACS approach for major depressive disorder: Initial findings from an open-label pilot study.
text: Theta oscillations are implicated in the pathophysiology of major depressive disorder (MDD) and represent a promising neuromodulation target. This study investigates individualized theta-frequency (ITF) transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) in adults with moderate-to-severe MDD, and reports on the initial evaluation of feasibility, tolerability, and clinical and neurophysiological outcomes. In this open-label pilot study, adults with MDD underwent a 20-session course of theta-frequency tACS (1.5 mA peak-to-peak; 20 min/session) applied bilaterally over the prefrontal cortex while performing working memory tasks. Theta stimulation frequency was individualized from pretreatment task-based electroencephalography (EEG) and recalibrated after 10 sessions. Montgomery-Asberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) and EEG were assessed at baseline, midpoint (2weeks), and endpoint (4weeks), with MADRS repeated at 4-week follow-up. Ten of 11 enrolled participants completed all 20 treatment sessions and were included in analyses. Reported side effects were mild and transient. MADRS scores decreased significantly from baseline to midpoint, endpoint, and follow-up. At endpoint, response and remission rates were 80% and 60%, respectively; at follow-up, rates were 80% and 70% respectively. Greater increases in individualized theta frequency (ITF) power were associated with greater reductions in MADRS scores, although no significant group-level changes in ITF power were observed. The open-label design, absence of a sham comparator, and small sample size warrant cautious interpretation of these initial observations, particularly given the potential influence of placebo and expectancy effects. This pilot evaluation of individualized theta-frequency tACS in MDD demonstrates the feasibility of this novel approach and provides preliminary clinical and neurophysiological observations to inform future sham-controlled trials.

title: Choroid plexus volume as a marker of chronotherapeutic responsiveness in major depressive disorder.
text: Circadian rhythm disruption is a core feature of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD). The choroid plexus (ChP), a circadian-regulated structure involved in cerebrospinal fluid production and immune signalling, has been previously associated with depression and may undergo structural changes in response to chronotherapeutics. The study included 25 patients with MDD and 25 matched healthy controls who underwent MRI. Patients received total sleep deprivation plus light therapy (TSD + LT), consisting of three 36-hour sleep deprivation cycles, each separated by a night of recovery sleep. LT was administered for 30 min every morning. Depressive symptoms, sleep quality, and chronotype were assessed through Beck's Depression Inventory (BDI), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire (MEQ), respectively. ChP volumes were extracted with FreeSurfer and normalized for intracranial volume. Effects of chronotherapeutics were assessed on BDI, PSQI, and ChP volumes, with treatment response as a between-subject factor. The efficacy of treatment was also investigated stratifying for chronotype. Also, group differences in ChP volume and associations with sleep and BDI scores were explored. TSD + LT reduced depressive symptoms and improved sleep quality, with changes in PSQI associated with symptom improvement. Eveningness predicted greater depressive symptom reduction. At baseline, responders already exhibited larger left ChP volume than controls. Following treatment, a treatment × response interaction emerged for right ChP volume, showing a significant reduction in responders. Finally, reductions in both right and left ChP volumes predicted clinical improvement, and sleep quality improvement predicted right ChP volume reduction. This is the first study showing that chronotherapy modulates ChP structure in MDD, suggesting a link between circadian dysregulation and ChP enlargement proportional to clinical improvement and predicted by sleep amelioration. ChP volume may represent a biomarker of treatment responsiveness and circadian realignment.

title: Simultaneous EEG-fMRI in major depressive disorder: A systematic review of brain networks, neurovascular coupling, and clinical correlates.
text: Simultaneous electroencephalography-functional magnetic resonance imaging (EEG-fMRI) offers unique potential to characterize brain network dysfunction and neurovascular coupling in major depressive disorder (MDD). However, the field lacks a rigorous synthesis restricted to strictly defined MDD populations with true multimodal integration. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420261292902), we searched PubMed, Scopus, CENTRAL, and Google Scholar (inception to March 2026) for simultaneous EEG-fMRI studies in adults (≥18 years) with MDD. We excluded subclinical samples, healthy-only populations, and sequential acquisitions to ensure diagnostic specificity. Primary outcomes were network dysfunction, neurovascular coupling, and clinical associations. Narrative synthesis was performed due to data paucity (<3 studies/outcome). Risk of bias was assessed using modified ROB2, ROBINS-I, and JBI tools. Nine studies (eight cohorts; N=377) met strict criteria. Two reports from one cohort investigating anhedonia via neurofeedback (Zotev et al.) showed moderate-to-strong correlations between EEG-fMRI metrics and severity (r = 0.47 and 0.69). Single-study findings reported effect sizes for anxiety (r = 0.74), depression change (r = -0.38 to 0.90), and rumination (r = 0.20). Analytical heterogeneity was substantial. Evidence certainty was low due to bias risk and imprecision. Small sample sizes, methodological fragmentation, and reliance on single cohorts for specific outcomes limit generalizability. Simultaneous EEG-fMRI identifies strong neurophysiological correlates (e.g., anhedonia, treatment response) in active contexts (e.g., neurofeedback, ketamine), but evidence for generalizable resting-state biomarkers remains insufficient. Future efforts must prioritize standardized pipelines and large-scale cohorts to transition this technique to a clinical biomarker.

title: Beyond monoamines: a multi-systems molecular framework for major depressive disorder.
text: For over five decades, the monoamine hypothesis has anchored the conceptual and pharmacological approach to major depressive disorder (MDD), yet nearly one-third of patients fail to achieve remission with standard antidepressants, and therapeutic response is delayed by weeks. This narrative review offers a critical synthesis of recent high-impact literature drawn on evidence from genomic, molecular, and translational studies across six domains: genomic architecture, epigenetic dysregulation, neuroinflammation, neurotrophic signalling, gut-brain axis, and rapid-acting antidepressant mechanisms, to construct a multi-systems framework of MDD pathophysiology and, as a secondary and explicitly scoped aim, to identify translational priorities for South Asian, particularly Indian, populations; the evidence reviewed is global in scope. A 2025 genome-wide association study (GWAS) of 688,808 cases identified 697 independent associations mapping to 635 genomic risk loci implicating glutamatergic, GABAergic, and neuropeptidergic systems. Environmental stressors converge on this genetic susceptibility through DNA methylation, histone modification, and non-coding RNA-mediated epigenetic reprogramming. An inflammatory MDD subgroup, characterised by kynurenine pathway disruption and microglial dysregulation, is of interest for patient stratification. Rapid-acting antidepressants proposed to act through TrkB-BDNF-dependent synaptic plasticity offer a mechanistic account of their fast onset, although the direct-binding theory awaits independent replication. Gut microbiome dysbiosis, particularly among neurotransmitter-producing taxa, further extends the pathophysiological map beyond the brain itself. Together, these findings support a shift from a unidimensional monoaminergic model to an integrated, multi-systems molecular framework of MDD. Realising the clinical potential of this framework will require validated precision biomarker panels, dedicated South Asian GWAS cohorts, and longitudinal multi-omics studies.

title: Investigating working memory and brain activation in major depressive disorder with and without insomnia: insights from functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS).
text: Major depressive disorder (MDD) frequently coexists with insomnia, a comorbidity that exacerbates cognitive deficits, particularly in working memory (WM). While previous research has established links between insomnia and impaired brain function, the barin functional indicators associated with WM deficits in MDD patients with insomnia remain unclear. This study explores cortical activation patterns in MDD patients with and without insomnia using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). A total of 55 MDD patients with insomnia and 67 without insomnia were recruited. Cortical activation during WM tasks was assessed using fNIRS, focusing on oxygenated hemoglobin (Oxy-Hb) concentration changes. Sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), depression severity was assessed using the Hamilton Depression Scale (HAMD), and cognitive function was assessed using the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status (RBANS). MDD patients with insomnia exhibited lower RBANS scores and reduced accuracy in medium-load WM tasks compared to non-insomnia patients. Additionally, fNIRS analysis revealed diminished Oxy-Hb concentrations in the bilateral dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) during medium-load tasks and in the left DLPFC during high-load tasks. Correlation analyses indicated that immediate memory scores negatively correlated with left DLPFC and bilateral medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) activation during medium-load tasks, while task accuracy negatively correlated with bilateral mPFC activation (p < 0.05). The presence of insomnia in MDD is associated with exacerbated WM deficits and altered prefrontal cortical activation, particularly in tasks with increased cognitive demand. These findings provide potential neurofunctional reference indicators, which may help offer auxiliary assessment means for MDD patients with insomnia. In addition, the sensitivity of fNIRS in detecting these neural brain activation differences suggest it may have potential as an exploratory screening tool for identifying subtypes of depression.

title: Genome-wide DNA methylation study uncovers epigenetic markers associated with early life stress in individuals with major depressive disorder.
text: Early life stress (ELS) is a significant risk factor for major depressive disorder (MDD); however, the epigenetic mechanisms underlying this association remain poorly characterized, partly due to the lack of trauma-stratified control groups in previous studies. We performed genome-wide DNA methylation profiling using Reduced-Representative Bisulfite Sequencing (RRBS) on whole blood samples from 90 adults divided into four groups: MDD with ELS (n = 30), MDD without ELS (n = 30), controls with ELS (n = 15), and controls without ELS (n = 15). Differentially methylated regions (DMRs) were identified employing MethylKit and DMRcate (≥5 CpGs, FDR < 0.05) and annotated via FUMA GENE2FUNC and clusterProfiler. Our analysis revealed 551, 581, and 479 DMRs in comparisons of MDD vs. control, MDD + ELS vs. control + ELS, and MDD non-ELS vs. control non-ELS, respectively. Core genes SELENOO, FASN, and THOC7 were consistently differentially methylated across all groups, reflecting shared mitochondrial, metabolic, and RNA-processing mechanisms. The MDD + ELS group demonstrated a higher DMR burden, particularly in regions associated with active promoter chromatin, with ELS-specific genes HIVEP3 and NRL exhibiting GWAS evidence linked to treatment-resistant depression and ADHD. Conversely, DMRs in MDD non-ELS were enriched in repressed chromatin states, with hypermethylation in loci within CAMK4 and CALM1 suggesting constitutive silencing of calcium-dependent neuronal signaling pathways. Our findings underscore the significant contribution of ELS to specific epigenetic changes associated with MDD, particularly in neurodevelopmental and stress-response pathways. In contrast, MDD without ELS exhibited a distinct methylation profile that affected synapses and synaptic plasticity. Our study, therefore, emphasizes the necessity of trauma-informed approaches in psychiatric research.

title: Prospective memory deficit associated with major depressive disorder: Causality, clinical impact, and potential molecular mechanisms.
text: Prospective memory (PM) impairment is frequently observed in major depressive disorder (MDD), yet its causal relationship, clinical impact, and molecular mechanisms remain unclear. To clarify causality between MDD and PM deficits, bidirectional mendelian randomization (MR) was conducted (MDD: n = 1639572; PM deficits: n = 152605). Genetic liability to MDD significantly increased the risk of PM deficits (OR = 1.045, P < 1 × 10-4), with a lack of evidence supporting a reverse causal effect. To assess clinical impact, we recruited 222 patients with MDD and 200 healthy controls (HCs). Patients with MDD showed significantly poorer PM performance across nearly all MIST subscales (PBonferroni < 0.05). Among 134 patients with follow-up, linear mixed-effects models revealed slower HAMD reduction in patients with PM deficits (z = 2.287, P = 0.022). PM performance showed no significant change after treatment (P = 0.117). To investigate potential mechanisms and therapeutics, shared targets for MDD and PM were identified through network pharmacology and summary-data-based MR, revealing Rap1 signaling as the top enriched pathway with eight core targets. Molecular docking showed relatively weak predicted affinities (mean > -7.5 kcal/mol) of commonly used antidepressants to these targets. Virtual screening of psychiatric compounds identified Hypericin, with strong affinity to the core targets (mean -9.06 kcal/mol). In conclusion, MDD may increase the risk of PM deficits, which are associated with poorer treatment response and show limited improvement following current antidepressant treatments. Rap1-related mechanisms may be involved, and Hypericin may be considered a compound for further investigation.
source: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics

title: Smartphone-Delivered Cognitive Behavioral Digital Therapeutic for Children and Adolescents With Major Depressive Disorder: Protocol for a Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
text: Depression is a leading contributor to morbidity and disability in children and adolescents. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a guideline-recommended first-line treatment, but access is constrained by therapist supply, distance, and stigma. Internet-based CBT is a scalable adjunct in adults, yet regulatory-grade evidence in Chinese pediatric samples remains limited. This trial will determine whether a smartphone-delivered CBT-based digital therapeutic is superior to a matched health-education placebo in reducing depressive symptoms in Chinese children and adolescents with major depressive disorder (MDD), and characterize its safety. This is a prospective, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled superiority trial at 4 tertiary-A hospitals in mainland China. Children and adolescents aged 8-17 years meeting DSM-5 (Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders [Fifth Edition]) criteria for current MDD without psychotic features and scoring above 30 on the Children's Depression Rating Scale-Revised (CDRS-R) at screening will be randomized 1:1 to the investigational digital therapeutic (Model WL-PD) or a visually matched health-education placebo. Both arms receive 8 weeks of structured content on an identical schedule; participants with CDRS-R ≥57 additionally receive open-label fluoxetine under weight-banded dosing. The primary end point is CDRS-R total-score reduction from baseline to week 8. Secondary end points include CDRS-R change at weeks 1 to 6; response and remission rates; Clinical Global Impression scores; the Children's Depression Inventory; the Conners' Parent Symptom Questionnaire; and a week-8 device-performance evaluation. Safety end points include adverse-event, serious adverse-event, and device-defect incidence. The planned sample of 214 participants (107 per arm) is powered at 80% to detect a between-arm difference of 4.6 CDRS-R points (assumed control SD 10.7) with a 1-sided α of .025 and 20% inflation for attrition. The primary analysis is an analysis of covariance on the full analysis set adjusting for baseline CDRS-R, severity category, fluoxetine exposure, and site; superiority is declared if the lower bound of the 2-sided 95% CI excludes zero, with a mixed model for repeated measures as a sensitivity analysis. The trial opened to enrollment in March 2026; recruitment is ongoing, with a planned close in December 2026. The last week-8 visit is expected in the first quarter of 2027, and the primary analysis the following year. The trial addresses 3 recognized gaps in the pediatric digital therapeutics literature: a rigorous, structurally matched blinded control condition, recruitment beyond a single site, and integration of guideline-concordant pharmacotherapy. Because recruitment is confined to tertiary hospitals and excludes participants with prominent suicidality or comorbidity, findings will apply to supervised use in specialist services rather than unselected community care. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2600120453; https://tinyurl.com/3xzaajhp. DERR1-10.2196/103430.

title: Integrated machine learning, single-cell RNA sequencing, and experimental validation for exploratory investigation of Fructus Aurantii in treating major depressive disorder.
text: Fructus Aurantii (FA), a Chinese herbal medicine, has been indicated to have antidepressant effects in our previous study. The potential mechanism of FA in the therapy of major depressive disorder (MDD) was explored through machine learning, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and experimental validation. We conducted differential analysis and WGCNA on the expression cohorts of MDD to determine differentially expressed genes and key module genes. FA-related targets were retrieved from multiple databases. Through the intersection of the aforementioned genes, candidate core targets were screened using the cytoHubba plug-in and machine learning methods. Subsequent analyses of these targets included clinical diagnostic evaluation, enrichment analysis, immune infiltration analysis, and molecular docking. scRNA-seq was used to explore the potential cellular mechanisms of MDD. Finally, RT-qPCR was employed to verify the gene expression level of the candidate core targets in the hippocampus. Four candidate core targets (ALOX5, PIK3CG, CHUK, and LRRK2) were determined using the cytoHubba plug-in and machine learning methods (LASSO regression, SVM-RFE, and Boruta). These targets exhibited notably elevated expression levels in the MDD group, and this finding was validated via RT-qPCR. The nomogram showed favorable value in clinical decision-making and diagnosis. Integrated analysis of signaling pathways and immune cells indicated that immune inflammation exerts an impact on MDD. Moreover, eosinophils and macrophages exhibited strong correlations with these targets and played crucial roles in immune inflammation. The active components of FA (limonin, auraptene, isosinensetin, nomilin, and luteolin) showed high binding affinity to these candidate core targets. Additionally, the expression of LRRK2 changed remarkably during the developmental stage of excitatory neurons. This research suggests that FA may exert its therapeutic effects through candidate core targets including ALOX5, PIK3CG, CHUK, and LRRK2, and key pathways associated with inflammation, immune dysregulation, and neuronal damage, providing a new perspective and important reference for subsequent MDD research and the development of therapeutic strategies.

title: Clinical and neural effects of a hybrid accelerated-maintenance iTBS protocol in adolescents with major depressive disorder.
text: Intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) has emerged as a safe and effective intervention for adolescents with major depressive disorder (MDD). While accelerated iTBS can induce rapid clinical improvement, intensive multi-day treatment schedules may present practical challenges for adolescents and their families, potentially affecting treatment adherence. This underscores the need for more flexible and feasible treatment strategies. This study evaluated the clinical efficacy of a hybrid accelerated-maintenance iTBS protocol, further explored treatment-related neural effects, and additionally examined the effects of accelerated iTBS beyond nonspecific factors. A total of 32 adolescents with MDD underwent a two-day accelerated phase followed by a four-week maintenance phase. Clinical and neuroimaging assessments were performed at baseline, after the accelerated phase, and at study completion, with 34 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HCs) providing baseline data for comparison. The results showed that Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) scores decreased significantly following treatment in adolescents with MDD (F (2,85) = 33.50, p < 0.001), with response and remission rates reaching 62.5 and 54.2%, respectively. Neuroimaging analyses at baseline revealed widespread alterations in amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations and functional connectivity across large-scale brain networks in adolescents with MDD. Following treatment, most alterations changed significantly and were no longer significantly different from those in HCs. In addition, supplementary analyses indicated significantly greater reductions in MADRS scores with active accelerated iTBS than with sham stimulation. These findings provide preliminary evidence for the utility of a hybrid accelerated-maintenance iTBS protocol in adolescents with MDD and insights into the neuroimaging mechanisms underlying treatment response.

title: Changes in brain structural connectivity networks are associated with electroconvulsive therapy efficacy in adolescents with major depressive disorder and suicidal ideation.
text: Suicide is a leading cause of death among adolescents with major depressive disorder (MDD). Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) effectively alleviates depressive symptoms, yet its underlying neural mechanisms remain unclear. 27 adolescents with MDD and SI and 32 demographically matched healthy controls were included. This study used structural magnetic resonance imaging and graph theory analyses to examine group differences in the global and nodal network topology at baseline and longitudinal changes within the MDD group following ECT. Linear mixed-effects models, correlation analysis, and machine learning were employed to further investigate the relationship between network topological properties and clinical symptoms. At baseline, adolescents with MDD exhibited reduced global normalized clustering and decreased nodal centrality across networks, with abnormalities predominantly in the limbic and sensorimotor systems. Following ECT, group differences in global network metrics were no longer significant, and topological abnormalities in networks related to emotional regulation and cognitive control were ameliorated. However, persistent topological disruptions in the sensorimotor and visual networks remained. Compare to topological metrics, machine learning models leveraging raw structural connectivity matrices demonstrated superior predictive performance for clinical efficacy. This study offers novel insights into the disorder's neurobiological mechanisms and the therapeutic effects of ECT.

title: Comparative efficacy and acceptability of antidepressants in the long-term treatment of major depressive disorder: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
text: Major depressive disorder carries high risks of relapse and chronicity, necessitating treatments that achieve and maintain response (sustained response). This study aimed to compare antidepressants on their ability to achieve sustained response, and on acceptability, by synthesising data from randomised controlled trials. For this systematic review and network meta-analysis, we searched the Cochrane Register, AMED, CINAHL, Embase, LILACS, MEDLINE, MEDLINE In-Progress, PsycINFO, the UK National Research Register, and regulatory agency websites from inception to March 27, 2026. We included double-blind randomised controlled trials that compared any of 21 antidepressants head-to-head or with placebo for long-term treatment (>12 weeks) of adult unipolar major depressive disorder. We included enrichment, non-enrichment, continuation, and continuation-extension designs, and extracted study-level data. We could not derive the sex or gender distribution of participants other than female and did not extract data on race or ethnicity. Primary outcomes were efficacy (sustained response rate) and acceptability (all-cause discontinuation). We synthesised data in random-effects pairwise and network meta-analyses to estimate pooled odds ratios (ORs), using fluoxetine as a reference in the ranked forest plots. The primary analysis included head-to-head continuation and continuation-extension design studies. Enrichment design studies were incorporated in the analysis using a chain-of-evidence approach. Risk-of-bias assessment was done using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. No people with lived experience were involved in the design, conduct, or interpretation of this study. From 54 231 records, 115 studies (30 428 participants; mean age 45·3 years [SD 8·5], 20 066 [66%] female) were included. In head-to-head continuation and continuation-extension design studies (35 studies; n=9888), sustained response differed across antidepressants. Escitalopram (OR 1·62, 95% CI 1·21-2·18), duloxetine (OR 1·57, 1·08-2·26), and agomelatine (OR 1·40, 1·06-1·85) showed higher sustained response rates than fluoxetine. Bupropion and reboxetine showed lower sustained response rates against four other antidepressants in the league table of pairwise comparisons. Escitalopram (OR 0·60, 0·43-0·83) and duloxetine (OR 0·64, 0·44-0·95) demonstrated lower all-cause discontinuation compared with fluoxetine, while reboxetine and milnacipran showed higher all-cause discontinuation against six and four other antidepressants, respectively, in the league table of pairwise comparisons. Sensitivity analyses incorporating enrichment-design studies corroborated these results. However, the certainty of evidence of the network meta-analysis results and the risk of bias in the included studies (19 [54%] of 35 had high risk of bias) might limit the reliability of the current findings. Antidepressants can differ in their efficacy for achieving sustained response and in their acceptability. These findings can inform the shared decision making for patients, prescribers, and carers in real-world practice. However, more head-to-head comparative studies are needed to provide reliable information about long-term effects of all licensed antidepressants. None.

title: Changes in wellbeing, self-compassion and alexithymia in a proof of principle trial with MDMA-assisted therapy for major depressive disorder.
text: Transdiagnostic factors such as emotion regulation, self-compassion, and alexithymia influence the development and outcome of psychiatric conditions, including major depressive disorder (MDD) and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). 3,4-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine-assisted therapy (MDMA-AT) has shown efficacy in reducing PTSD and depressive symptoms. This study examined MDMA-AT effects on alexithymia, self-compassion, and well-being in MDD, assessing durability and links to long-term outcomes. Data were drawn from an open-label MDMA-AT trial (EudraCT 2021-000805-26) including twelve participants with moderate to severe MDD (baseline MADRS M(SD) = 29.6(4.9)). Participants received two MDMA sessions with manualized psychotherapy (three preparatory, six integration). Outcomes were assessed at baseline, post-treatment (8 weeks), and long-term follow-up (≥3 months) using the Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20), Self-Compassion Scale (SCS), and Warwick-Edinburgh Mental Wellbeing Scale (WEMWBS). Changes were analyzed with linear mixed models; estimated marginal means and post-hoc comparisons explored time effects. MDMA-AT significantly improved alexithymia, self-compassion, and well-being. TAS-20 decreased by -11.75 post-treatment and -16.42 at follow-up (both p < 0.001). SCS increased by 0.73 post-treatment (p = 0.017) and 1.07 at follow-up (p = 0.001). WEMWBS improved by 17.30 at both timepoints (p < 0.001). All SCS subscales improved; common humanity and isolation reached significance only at follow-up. Improvements were driven by therapy responders (9/12). Eight participants had at least borderline alexithymia at baseline; none did at follow-up. Self-compassion shifted from seven low and one high at baseline to seven high and one low at follow-up. MDMA-AT for MDD produced lasting improvements in alexithymia, self-compassion, and well-being, supporting its potential for durable psychological recovery beyond symptom reduction.

title: Mitochondrial Quality Control and Apoptotic Thresholds in Major Depressive Disorder: A Structured Narrative Review.
text: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is clinically heterogeneous, and many patients do not achieve sustained remission with monoaminergic treatments. Mitochondrial dysfunction has been associated with chronic stress, impaired synaptic function, altered cellular energetics, and neuronal vulnerability, but evidence concerning mitochondrial dynamics, mitophagy, redox imbalance, calcium signaling, and intrinsic apoptosis remains distributed across experimental systems. This structured narrative review integrates human brain and peripheral studies, patient-derived cellular evidence, animal models, and general cell biology. We propose the mitochondrial quality control-mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MQC-MOMP) threshold model as a conceptual framework, not an experimentally established disease mechanism. In this model, cumulative failure of mitochondrial repair and clearance may shift stress responses toward Bax/Bak-dependent MOMP and caspase activation. Human findings are largely associative and do not establish widespread mitochondria-driven neuronal apoptosis in living patients with MDD; mechanistic support is strongest in preclinical and cellular models. The framework therefore differs from prior topic-based reviews by organizing heterogeneous evidence according to evidence source, certainty, and proximity to clinical translation. Here we highlight testable priorities for biomarker validation, patient stratification, cell-type-resolved studies, longitudinal cohorts, and mechanism-based interventions.

title: Multi-Omics Mendelian Randomization Prioritizes Candidate Druggable Genes for Major Depressive Disorder.
text: This study aimed to prioritize candidate druggable genes for major depressive disorder (MDD) using Mendelian randomization (MR) integrated with expression (eQTL) and protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL) data. We conducted a systematic MR analysis combining cis-eQTL and cis-pQTL data from blood and brain tissues to assess the causal effects of druggable genes on MDD, using FinnGen R9 GWAS summary statistics. Bayesian colocalization analysis confirmed shared genetic variants, while sensitivity analyses (MR-Egger, weighted median, MR-PRESSO) tested robustness. A phenome-wide MR (Phe-MR) assessed broader trait associations. To evaluate translational potential, we mapped candidate genes to known drugs using DrugBank, ChEMBL, and ClinicalTrials.gov.Six candidate druggable genes (MAPK3, PSMB9, SIGLEC9, MST1, BTN3A1, and TAPBP) showed significant associations with MDD across multiple eQTL and pQTL datasets. These genes are involved in biological processes related to neuroinflammation, immune regulation, and apoptosis. Colocalization analyses supported shared genetic signals between the identified genes and MDD, while phenome-wide analyses identified associations with additional diseases and traits that may be relevant for future translational research. Through MR analysis, six candidate druggable genes were prioritized from 6889 potential druggable genes as significantly associated with MDD. Among them, MAPK3, MST1, and SIGLEC9 showed consistent evidence across multiple analyses and emerged as genetically supported candidate targets for future investigation.

title: Severe toxicity following supratherapeutic co‑ingestion of duloxetine and dexzopiclone in a young patient with major depressive disorder: a case report.
text: A 23-year-old female with major depressive disorder (MDD), non-suicidal self-injury and generalized somatic pain was treated with duloxetine hydrochloride enteric-coated capsules, quetiapine fumarate tablets, and aripiprazole orally disintegrating tablets, with significant pain relief. Dexzopiclone tablets were added for insomnia, and all medications were kept by her mother. Despite compliance with medication, the patient had persistent suicidal ideation and secretly ingested 4500 mg duloxetine and 63 mg dexzopiclone on February 18, 2021. She was rushed to hospital 3.5 h later and received emergency treatment including oxygen inhalation, gastric lavage and high-dose vitamin B6/C infusion. Combined with psychological suggestion and cognitive therapy, she recovered and was discharged 12 days later. At the 4.5-year follow-up (September 2025), the patient had discontinued lurasidone and quetiapine, both of which were started during index hospitalization; she demonstrated normal daily functioning with no recurrent suicidal ideation or self-injury. To our knowledge, severe toxicity from co-ingestion of supratherapeutic doses of duloxetine and dexzopiclone has been rarely documented; this report details the clinical management and differential diagnosis strategies for this rare drug-combination toxicity.

title: Large language models advance single-cell transcriptomics in major depressive disorder.
text: Major depressive disorder (MDD) exhibits substantial heterogeneity, posing challenges for its diagnosis and treatment. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has emerged as a powerful tool for delineating cellular programs in neuronal and immune populations implicated in MDD pathogenesis. Advances in large language models (LLMs) are now enhancing single-cell analysis by improving annotation, clustering, regulatory network inference, and in silico perturbation to prioritize druggable targets. Integration with proteomic, metabolomic, epigenomic, and spatial data further clarifies disease mechanisms and potential biomarkers. Key challenges including data heterogeneity, model interpretability, computational scale, and ethical data usage remain to be addressed through rigorous benchmarks and validation to accelerate translation. Collectively, integration of LLMs with single-cell technologies provides a framework for more precise, cell-resolved hypothesis generation in MDD, while prospective validation of patient-level clinical utility remains a key next step.

title: The effects of pulse dosing on the clinical trajectory of rTMS and iTBS: A re-analysis of two sham-controlled studies in major depressive disorder.
text: The dose-response relationship in repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) remains unclear. Although increasing the number of pulses may accelerate clinical improvement, they do not consistently yield superior antidepressant endpoints, and placebo responses in neuromodulation trials may vary with treatment intensity. We conducted a secondary analysis of pooled data from two randomized controlled trials (N = 177) involving patients with major depressive disorder. Active treatment arms included 10-Hz rTMS and intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS), each delivered with different numbers of pulses per session (pps). Linear mixed-effects models evaluated interactions among time, treatment type (active vs. sham), and pulses per session (pps) on changes in Hamilton Depression Rating Scale - 17 Items (HAMD-17) scores over two weeks. The results revealed a significant time × pulses per session (pps) interaction (β = -0.001, p = 0.033), suggesting that more pulses per session may be associated with clinical improvement. However, this trend did not differ significantly between the active and sham groups (p = 0.270). Furthermore, no significant differences were observed between iTBS and rTMS. Our findings suggested a potential nonspecific therapeutic effect associated with the number of pulses per session, which might influence symptom trajectories during the early stages of rTMS and iTBS treatments. This provides a nuanced understanding of how stimulation parameters contribute to the trajectory of recovery in major depressive disorder, offering valuable insights for optimizing clinical treatment parameters.

title: Lifestyle-Based Interventions for Major Depressive Disorder and Their Role Alongside Antidepressant Treatment: A Systematic Review.
text: Major depressive disorder (MDD) remains disabling despite effective pharmacotherapy, and many patients experience an incomplete response or residual symptoms. This systematic review evaluated randomized trials of structured exercise or mind-body exercise, sleep/circadian and bright-light interventions, whole-diet interventions, and multicomponent lifestyle programs delivered alongside antidepressant treatment in adults with current MDD. PubMed, Europe PMC, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception through September 15, 2026, with supplementary citation searching of eligible reports and relevant reviews. The electronic searches identified 1,310 records. After the removal of 333 duplicate bibliographic records and one non-usable record, 976 records underwent screening. Thirty-eight reports were assessed at full text. Following eligibility assessment and final verification, 26 eligible reports remained from the original search, and eight additional eligible reports were identified through supplementary citation searching. The final review included 34 reports representing 29 independent randomized studies.
