After adjustment, lower 25-hydroxyvitamin D was not clearly associated with severe pneumonia. Vitamin D deficiency was highly prevalent among hospitalized children with CAP, but admission 25-hydroxyvitamin D was not clearly associated with pneumonia severity. The relatively small hospitalized cohort and wide confidence intervals limit the strength and generalizability of these findings. Larger prospective studies with more complete assessment of nutritional, seasonal, clinical, and socioeconomic confounders are needed. Vitamin D plays an important role in bone health and may also influence the immune system. We studied 100 children who were hospitalized with community-acquired pneumonia to determine whether low vitamin D levels were associated with more severe illness. Vitamin D deficiency was common in both children with severe pneumonia and those with mild or moderate pneumonia. Children with severe pneumonia had somewhat lower vitamin D levels, but the difference was not statistically clear. After considering several other factors, lower vitamin D levels were not clearly associated with severe pneumonia. Vitamin D levels were also not clearly related to admission to the pediatric intensive care unit or the length of hospitalization. Because this was a relatively small study involving only hospitalized children, larger studies are needed before firm conclusions can be made about whether vitamin D status influences the severity of childhood pneumonia.

title: Clinical validation of a novel multiplex real-time PCR for diagnosing community-acquired pneumonia in the emergency department: a promising diagnostic tool for Mycoplasma pneumoniae.
text: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) is a global public health burden with high morbidity, but timely diagnosis is hindered by limitations of conventional methods. We validated a novel multiplex real-time PCR (mRT-PCR) for CAP diagnosis in the emergency department, focusing on Mycoplasma pneumoniae (M. pneumoniae). A retrospective cohort of 371 CAP patients (2019-2021) from the Chinese PLA General Hospital was enrolled. The panel targeted 85 pathogens (40 bacteria, 18 viruses, 17 fungi, 10 other) plus 8 resistance genes, with a turnaround time (TAT) under 4 h and a cost of approximately US$100 per test. mRT-PCR showed performance comparable to mNGS for common pathogens (concordance >69% for bacteria/fungi) and high concordance with the final clinical diagnosis. Notably, it detected M. pneumoniae in 36.7% (136/371) of cases, outperforming conventional methods by identifying 204 exclusive positives (55.0% of cohort), with M. pneumoniae (40%) and viruses (30%) predominating. Polymicrobial infections occurred in 36.1% of cases; M. pneumoniae co-infections (38 cases) showed elevated neutrophils and reduced lymphocytes vs. single infections. An independent reference standard analysis excluding both index tests showed that 24.1% (210/873) of calls were independently corroborated - high for influenza, SARS-CoV-2 and M. pneumoniae, lower for S. pneumoniae, consistent with the limited sensitivity of sputum culture. Unlike conventional syndromic panels such as FilmArray, which profile fewer targets without concurrent resistance-gene detection, this mRT-PCR combines broad coverage with rapid TAT and low cost, making it promising for timely CAP diagnosis, particularly in resource-limited settings and for targeted therapy.

title: Right ventricular function across different non-invasive respiratory support strategies in severe community-acquired pneumonia.
text: Right ventricular (RV) systolic impairment is clinically relevant in acute respiratory failure, but its relationship with respiratory support modality in severe community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) outside the intensive care unit (ICU) is poorly defined. To compare RV longitudinal systolic performance and hospital length of stay (LOS) among patients receiving non-invasive ventilation (NIV), high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC), or Venturi-mask oxygen therapy. In this single-centre prospective observational study, adults with severe CAP (Pneumonia Severity Index class IV-V) requiring high-concentration oxygen or non-invasive respiratory support were enrolled. The modality was selected in the emergency department according to the treating physician's clinical and gas-exchange assessment. Echocardiography was performed shortly after ward admission while patients remained on the initial support modality. Seventy patients were included (NIV, n = 21; HFNC, n = 22; Venturi mask, n = 27). Baseline demographic and cardiometabolic characteristics were comparable across groups. TAPSE and lateral tricuspid annular systolic velocity (S') showed a graded pattern, with the lowest values during NIV, intermediate values during HFNC, and the highest values with the Venturi mask (p < 0.001 for both). Mean LOS was 27.8 ± 5.0, 27.4 ± 2.9, and 15.2 ± 4.0 days, respectively (p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, age and respiratory support modality were associated with LOS. RV systolic performance and LOS differed across clinically selected respiratory support groups. These associations may reflect clinical severity rather than device-related effects. These findings reinforce the often-overlooked clinical importance of RV assessment in acute respiratory failure, extending observations from ARDS cohorts to severe CAP outside the ICU.
source: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care

title: Real-world use of procalcitonin for antimicrobial stewardship in severe community-acquired pneumonia.
text: Real-world evidence is limited regarding the use and impact of procalcitonin (PCT) on antibiotic duration in severe community-acquired pneumonia (SCAP) patients. A retrospective cohort study of adult patients with SCAP (defined by modified American Thoracic Society [ATS] criteria) to 12 hospitals between November 2022 and June 2025. We analyzed clinical characteristics and estimated the association between PCT testing within 24 hours of hospital admission and antibiotic duration, and between low (<.5 µg/L) and high (≥.5 µg/L) PCT values and antibiotic duration. Clinical stability was determined based on ATS criteria (temperature <100 °F with ≤1 sign of instability within 24 hours of admission). Among 1,553 SCAP admissions, 325 (21%) were clinically stable on admission and 924 patients (59.5%) had PCT testing within 24 hours; 452 (48.9%) of PCTs were low. Clinical stability was not associated with testing. PCT testing was associated with fewer antibiotic days (mean 6.9 vs 7.4 days adjusted mean difference, -.5 days, 95% CI: -.8, -.3), particularly in stable (mean 6.6 vs 7.3 days, adjusted mean difference, -.8 days, 95% CI: -1, -.1) versus unstable patients (mean 7.2 vs 7.5 days, adjusted mean difference, -.4 days, 95% CI: -.8, -.05). Low PCT values were associated with shorter antibiotic durations than high values (mean 6.5 vs 7.6 days, adjusted mean difference, -1.1 days, 95% CI: -1.9, -.3). PCT testing was associated with shorter antibiotic duration, especially among stable patients, but was performed without regard to clinical stability. Reserving PCT testing for stable patients may improve efficiency.

title: Effect of clarithromycin on the circulating inflammatory proteome in community-acquired pneumonia: a secondary analysis of the ACCESS trial.
text: The ACCESS randomized double-blind controlled trial in hospitalized adults with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) showed that adding clarithromycin to standard-of-care therapy accelerated clinical recovery within the first 72 hours after the commencement of treatment and reduced progression to organ dysfunction. Does clarithromycin treatment modulate the circulating inflammatory protein profile in CAP, and can inflammatory endotypes identify patient subgroups with distinct clinical responses? Serum samples obtained from ACCESS trial patients at baseline and 72 hours were profiled using the Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel. Patients were grouped by treatment arm and by achievement of the trial's composite primary endpoint. After quality control, 70 proteins from 394 paired samples across 197 patients were analyzed to assess differential expression within and between groups over time, evaluate associations with clinical outcomes, and identify immune endotypes using unsupervised clustering. IL6 was selectively downregulated on day 4 in the clarithromycin arm, whereas IFN-γ, CXCL9, CXCL10, and SCF decreased over time across both treatment arms, consistent with resolution of inflammation. Among patients achieving the primary endpoint, IL6, CXCL9, CXCL10, and IFN-γ were suppressed only in clarithromycin-treated individuals. Clustering consistently identified two inflammatory endotypes with comparable SOFA, but distinct RSS scores. The endotype with lower RSS demonstrated higher IFN-γ and globally elevated inflammatory protein expression; in that endotype 90-day mortality was decreased with clarithromycin treatment. Clarithromycin exerts measurable immunomodulatory effects in CAP, characterized by attenuation of pro-inflammatory cytokines, particularly IL6. The identification of distinct inflammatory endotypes suggests biological heterogeneity in CAP and supports future investigation of endotype-guided approaches to identify patients most likely to benefit from immunomodulatory therapies. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04724044, EudraCT 2020-004452-15.

title: S100A8/A9 as a biomarker for differentiating pulmonary tuberculosis from community-acquired pneumonia in children: a multicenter cohort study in China.
text: Differentiating pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) from community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) in children remains a significant diagnostic challenge. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic value of serum S100A8/A9 in pediatric populations. This multicenter prospective study enrolled 1,629 children aged 0∼≤ 18 years with definitive diagnostic classifications, including a discovery cohort (n = 1,092) and a validation cohort (n = 537). Participants were stratified into three groups: PTB (Confirmed, Unconfirmed), CAP (Viral, Bacterial, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Mixed), and healthy controls (HC). Serum S100A8/A9 levels were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and diagnostic performance was assessed using ROC analysis. In both cohorts, S100A8/A9 levels were markedly lower in PTB than in CAP but higher than in healthy controls. (both p < 0.001). For distinguishing PTB from CAP, S100A8/A9 achieved AUC values of 0.916 (95% CI: 0.895-0.937, sensitivity 87.1%, specificity 81.8%) in the discovery cohort and 0.932 (95% CI: 0.906-0.958, sensitivity 87.5%, specificity 86.4%) in the validation cohort. Compared with all CAP etiological subgroups, PTB children had the lowest S100A8/A9 levels, with the highest AUC of 0.954 for PTB vs. Mycoplasma pneumoniae CAP. Age-stratified analysis revealed excellent discriminatory performance in children aged 5-18 years (AUC = 0.955 for PTB versus overall CAP). but impaired in children under 5 years (AUC = 0.838 for PTB versus overall CAP), with lower sensitivity (57.4%) for discriminating PTB from Viral-CAP. Furthermore, a concentration-dependent distribution was observed, with higher S100A8/A9 levels associated with a decreasing proportion of PTB and an increasing proportion of CAP. In children aged 5-18 years, levels < 1,000 ng/mL were predominantly PTB (92.1%), and levels > 1,900 ng/mL were highly predictive of CAP (96.8%). Serum S100A8/A9 is a promising potential biomarker for distinguishing pediatric PTB from CAP, characterized by age-related distribution and concentration-dependent diagnostic pattern.

title: Acute Kidney Injury in Hospitalized Patients with Community-Acquired Pneumonia: Frequency, Factors Associated with AKI, and Clinical Outcomes.
text: Background: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) is a common infectious disease associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a frequent complication of CAP and may adversely affect clinical outcomes. This study aimed to determine the frequency of AKI and identify factors associated with AKI in hospitalized patients with CAP. Methods: This retrospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary care university hospital in Türkiye and included patients aged >18 years hospitalized with CAP between July 2024 and July 2025. Only patients initially admitted to the general ward were included. Patients receiving dialysis for end-stage renal disease, those with active malignancy, those receiving immunosuppressive therapy, and those with incomplete data were excluded. Demographic characteristics, vital signs, laboratory findings, comorbidities, smoking status, and medication histories were recorded. AKI was defined according to KDIGO criteria using the closest clinically stable pre-admission serum creatinine value obtained within 7-365 days before hospitalization as baseline. Results: Among 161 patients, AKI was identified in 60 (37.3%), including 43 patients who fulfilled the KDIGO criteria at hospital admission and 17 who developed AKI during hospitalization. Eight patients with AKI (13.3%) required hemodialysis, although none became permanently dialysis-dependent. Patients with AKI had longer hospital stays (p = 0.038) and a greater need for intensive care (p = 0.028). They were older and had higher respiratory rates, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), and red cell distribution width (RDW) values and lower diastolic blood pressure. DM and CKD were more common in the AKI group. In multivariable analysis, confusion (adjusted OR 5.03, 95% CI 1.01-25.02; p = 0.048), CKD (adjusted OR 6.00, 95% CI 1.28-28.13; p = 0.023), and higher BUN levels (adjusted OR 1.095 per 1 mg/dL increase, 95% CI 1.046-1.146; p < 0.001) were independently associated with AKI. These associations were retained in a Firth penalized logistic regression sensitivity analysis. Conclusions: AKI was common among hospitalized patients with CAP and was associated with longer hospital stay and greater intensive care utilization. Confusion, pre-existing CKD, and elevated BUN levels were independently associated with AKI, whereas DM was not independently associated after multivariable adjustment. Given that most AKI cases were already present at hospital admission, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than predictors of incident AKI.

title: Development of a novel diagnostic tool for community-acquired pneumonia based on microbial community characteristics.
text: The lung microbiota plays a key role in pneumonia. A correct diagnosis in the early stage helps treatment and limits severity progression of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). There were 42 patients with CAP and 20 controls. Amplicon bacterial 16S sequencing from bronchoalveolar lavage fluid samples revealed indicator genera by linear discriminant analysis effect size, random forest and ROC analyses. The abundance of bacteria was combined with laboratory inflammatory indexes to construct logistic regression models for CAP diagnosis. The final predictive model with a lower Akaike information criterion (AIC) was internally validated by bootstrap resampling. After confirming lower respiratory tract (LRT) microbiome dysbiosis in CAP patients, we identified five indicator genera: Moraxella (M), Prevotella_1 (P), Lautropia (L), Neisseria (N), and Fusobacterium (F). Their combined effect was incorporated by calculation of the joint prediction probability (PRE) based on their relative abundances as PRE = 1 / (1 + EXP (-4.39 + 18.96 M + 9.30P - 5.38 L + 0.89 N + 0.70F)). A nomogram was constructed for CAP diagnosis that incorporated PRE with serum levels of CRP (cut-off ≥5.23 mg/L) and Neutrophil % (cut-off ≥66.05%). After internal validation, this nomogram showed satisfactory diagnostic performance with the bootstrap-corrected AUC of 0.927 and a well-fitting calibration curve. The LRT microbiome was altered in CAP patients. Indicator genera were shown to have the potential to serve as diagnosis biomarkers in the constructed predictive model. These results may provide further clues for the microbial pathogenesis, optimized diagnostics and new therapeutic targets of CAP.
source: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases

title: Etiological characteristics and infection-related biomarkers in patients with severe community-acquired pneumonia in the emergency department: A retrospective cohort study.
text: Severe community-acquired pneumonia (SCAP) remains a leading cause of infectious disease mortality worldwide. Timely identification of causative pathogens and appropriate antimicrobial therapy are critical determinants of patient outcomes. This retrospective cohort study investigated the etiological features of SCAP and their relationship with infection-related biomarkers, including C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), D-dimer (D-D), white blood cell count (WBC), and neutrophil percentage (NEUT), in an emergency department setting. A total of 146 patients with SCAP admitted to Tianjin Medical University General Hospital between March 2018 and March 2019 were included. Pathogen identification was performed through sputum or bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) cultures. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method. A total of 154 bacterial strains were isolated from 146 patients. Gram-negative bacteria predominated (145 strains, 94.2%), followed by Gram-positive bacteria (8 strains, 5.2%). The most frequently isolated pathogens were Klebsiella pneumoniae (25.3%), Acinetobacter baumannii (20.1%), and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (13.6%). Extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing strains were identified in 17 of 39 K. pneumoniae isolates (43.6%). High-risk clones of K. pneumoniae ST11, ST15, ST307, A. baumannii ST2, P. aeruginosa ST235 were detected in this study. Cefoperazone-sulbactam demonstrated low resistance rates in K. pneumoniae (7.7%), A. baumannii (9.7%), Enterobacter cloacae (8.3%), and P. aeruginosa (14.3%). Abnormal PCT levels were associated with higher proportions of K. pneumoniae and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia infections. Elevated CRP, D-D, WBC, and NEUT levels were more frequently observed in patients infected with K. pneumoniae and A. baumannii. Gram-negative bacteria, particularly K. pneumoniae and A. baumannii, are the predominant pathogens in SCAP. Infection-related biomarkers, especially PCT, show promise in predicting specific etiologies and may guide empirical antimicrobial selection.

title: Toward precision host-directed immunomodulation in community-acquired pneumonia: a proposed endotype-target-natural-product framework and a roadmap for validation in human lung organoids.
text: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) still causes high mortality despite effective antibiotics. Much of this death is driven by a dysregulated host immune response rather than by the pathogen itself, and antimicrobial resistance deepens the problem. Host-directed therapy has accordingly shifted toward precision immunomodulation, yet its benefit appears conditional on the inflammatory state. Stratification by a single inflammatory axis such as C-reactive protein (CRP) separates broad prognostic subgroups, but it does not indicate which effector pathway to target or which agent to use; we designate this limitation, as a conceptual shorthand rather than a validated threshold, the "CRP ceiling." Existing reviews treat natural-product host-directed therapy, CAP inflammatory endotyping, and human lung organoid modeling separately; the gap we address is the absence of a framework that connects them. Integrating these three fields, we propose, as a hypothesis-generating rather than a validated scheme, an endotype-target-natural-product framework for bacterial CAP. We first outline the interventable core of CAP immunopathology across the inflammasome, neutrophil extracellular trap (NET), and resolution axes, together with the pathogen-specific virulence that biases them; we then propose that the multi-target pharmacology of natural products may suit candidate endotypes driven by several co-activated nodes, where single-target agents have often failed, while noting that their comparatively favorable toxicity is itself a hypothesis rather than an established class property; and we position human lung organoids as a promising human-relevant platform, alongside complementary systems, that could test endotype-, compound-, and pathogen-specific hypotheses and provide a roadmap for validation before clinical translation. The framework is intended to complement, not replace, pathogen-directed treatment, and to reframe host-directed therapy from uniform anti-inflammation toward modulation matched to mechanism, pathogen, and patient. The principal challenges concern immune-competent organoids, validated pathway-level endotype biomarkers, and standardized characterization of multi-component natural products.

title: Epidemiology, risk factors and clinical outcome of community-acquired pneumonia in severely immunosuppressed patients: a comprehensive analysis from the multinational, prospective CAPNETZ Cohort.
text: Despite growing evidence that immunosuppression (IS) influences aetiology and prognosis of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), there remains a lack of data from representative multicentre studies. The multinational prospective CAPNETZ study includes patients with CAP and HIV since 2017, and with other causes of IS since 2020. We present the first comprehensive analysis of patients with CAP and IS (HIV with low CD4 cells, systemic steroids, immunosuppressive drugs, antineoplastic treatment, neutropenia, primary immunodeficiency, transplantation, haematological neoplasia) included within CAPNETZ until December 2023. IS cases were matched 1:1 with non-IS patients. The primary end-point was 30-day mortality and/or organ replacement therapy. Additionally, cases of CAP caused by non-core respiratory pathogens (NCRPs) according to an international consensus were evaluated. Univariate and multivariate risk factor analyses and evaluation of predictive scores by receiver operating characteristic analysis were performed. We included 232 patients with IS, most commonly after antineoplastic therapy (37.5%), systemic steroids (36.2%) and immunosuppressive drugs (35.8%). 10.3% reached the primary end-point. Overall, IS was not associated with prognosis compared to matched non-IS patients, but patients with immunosuppressive drugs had a significantly lower risk. The qSOFA, CRB-65 and CURB-65 scores showed limited prediction (area under the curve 0.57-0.64) and insufficient sensitivity for the primary end-point. CAP caused by NCRPs occurred in 16.4% in IS and was associated with transplantation, previous anti-infective treatment and intensive care unit admission, but SARS-CoV-2, Haemophilus influenzae and Streptococcus pneumoniae were the most common pathogens in both groups. This study demonstrates the relevance and heterogeneity of CAP in IS and highlights the need for individualised risk stratification and treatment.

title: External validation of a clinical prediction score for melioidosis among patients with community-acquired pneumonia: a substudy of the prospective multicentre MISSION cohort.
text: Pulmonary melioidosis may be clinically indistinguishable from other causes of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), delaying appropriate microbiological investigation and antimicrobial therapy. A four-variable clinical prediction score incorporating monsoon-season presentation, diabetes mellitus, shock at presentation, and extrapulmonary focal abscesses was previously developed to identify melioidosis among patients with CAP. We aimed to externally validate this score in a prospective multicentre cohort and explore whether its performance could be improved by adding readily available predictors. This was a nested substudy of the prospective, multicentre, hospital-based MISSION study conducted across 15 tertiary-care centres in India between 1 January 2023 and 31 December 2025. Hospitalised adults with diabetes mellitus or chronic kidney disease who met predefined CAP criteria were eligible. Participants were excluded if one or more score variables could not be reliably ascertained at presentation, defined as clinical information available before microbiological confirmation. The original score was applied without refitting. Discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and sensitivity and specificity were calculated at prespecified cut-offs. An exploratory modified score was developed using independent predictors identified through multivariable logistic regression. Of 1,418 participants in the parent cohort who met the predefined CAP syndrome definition, 78 were excluded because one or more score variables could not be reliably ascertained at presentation. The final validation cohort included 1,340 participants, of whom 87 (6.5%) had culture-confirmed melioidosis CAP. The original score demonstrated moderate discrimination, with an AUC of 0.718 (95% CI 0.654-0.781). At a cut-off of ≥4, sensitivity was 72.4%, and specificity was 56.4%; at ≥5, sensitivity was 48.3%, and specificity was 86.4%. Extrapulmonary focal abscesses (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 20.56, 95% CI 10.82-39.05), diabetes mellitus (aOR 2.94, 95% CI 1.36-6.37), male sex (aOR 2.39, 95% CI 1.32-4.33), high-risk occupation (aOR 2.37, 95% CI 1.43-3.93), and shock at presentation (aOR 2.30, 95% CI 1.31-4.05) were independently associated with melioidosis CAP. An exploratory modified score incorporating these variables had an apparent AUC of 0.770 (95% CI 0.711 to 0.828). At a cut-off of ≥3, sensitivity was 63.2% and specificity was 81.4%. The original four-variable score demonstrated moderate discrimination when externally validated among high-risk hospitalised adults with CAP. A cut-off of ≥4 may support screening, whereas ≥5 provides greater specificity but misses more than half of melioidosis cases. The exploratory modified score showed modestly higher apparent discrimination, and requires independent external validation before clinical use.
source: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases

title: Antibiotic Choice for Community-Acquired Pneumonia in Children With Medical Complexity.
text: There are no guideline recommendations for antibiotic choice for community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) in children with medical complexity (CMC). We compared broad- vs narrow-spectrum antibiotics in CMC hospitalized with nonsevere CAP. This cohort study was conducted using target trial emulation within an academic health system. We included hospitalizations from January 2016 to April 2024 with International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10) codes for CAP and complex chronic conditions among children aged 3 months to 21 years who received 3 or more days of antibiotics. We excluded children with severe/complicated CAP, chronic pulmonary conditions, sickle cell disease, tracheostomies, immunosuppression, other bacterial infections, or recent CAP admission. The exposure was initial broad-spectrum antibiotics (CAP antibiotics other than aminopenicillins) within 12 hours of presentation. The primary outcome was time to discharge, censored at day 10. Secondary outcomes were progression to severe CAP and 30-day CAP-related revisits. To mitigate confounding, we applied inverse probability of treatment weighting in outcome models, including a Royston-Parmar flexible survival model for time to discharge, and logistic regression for binary outcomes. A total of 847 encounters (749 patients) were included. After weighting and trimming, 742 encounters remained with adequate covariate balance. Compared with the narrow-spectrum group, the broad-spectrum group demonstrated no significant differences in time to discharge (hazard ratio, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.68-1.04), progression to severe CAP (odds ratio [OR], 1.29; 95% CI, 0.7-2.4), or 30-day CAP-related revisits (OR, 0.39; 95% CI, 0.1-1.2). In CMC hospitalized with nonsevere CAP, initial broad-spectrum antibiotics did not improve clinical outcomes compared with narrow-spectrum antibiotics, supporting the use of aminopenicillins for nonsevere CAP in many CMC.

title: Patient and author diversity and representation in studies supporting the European Respiratory Society/European Society of Intensive Care Medicine/European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases/Asociación Latinoamericana de Tórax severe community-acquired pneumonia guidelines.
text: Insufficient diversity is common among patients and authors in studies supporting guidelines. We hypothesized that the latest severe community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) guidelines suffered from such bias. We reviewed all original studies supporting the latest severe CAP guidelines. We assessed whether there were language restrictions in the search for studies to be included in each recommendation and recorded the following: the proportion of female patients included in the studies; ethnicity (when available); year of publication; and study location, which was classified by income in accordance with the World Bank classification. We also compiled data on the sex and affiliation of the first and last authors. The guidelines included 115 references in eight sections; 74 unique references supported the recommendations. There was language restriction in the selection of studies in 3 of 8 questions. The proportion of female patients ranged from 4.7% to 70.5% (mean, 36%). Most of the patients were White (72.2-91.2%), and 80.5% of the studies were conducted in high-income countries. Only 6 (5.2%) of the 115 references included patients from low- or middle-income countries. Most of the first and last authors were male (75.6-88.3%) and were based in high-income countries (96.1%). The studies supporting the severe CAP guidelines were found to have insufficient diversity and representativeness of patients, sex, and country of origin of the authors. To enhance the generalizability of severe CAP guidelines, strategies must be devised to increase the diversity of patients and authors.

title: Time to recovery and its predictors among pediatric patients with severe community-acquired pneumonia admitted to public general hospitals in Tigray, Ethiopia, 2025: A prospective follow-up study.
text: Globally, pneumonia is a major cause of illness and death in children, with over 1,400 cases per 100,000 children each year. In sub-Saharan Africa, pneumonia is responsible for approximately 172 deaths per 1,000 live births. Ethiopia has the fifth highest mortality rate from pneumonia among children under five, especially severe community-acquired pneumonia. In Ethiopia, there are limited prospective follow-up studies on time to recovery and its predictors among pediatric patients with severe community-acquired pneumonia. However, no prospective follow-up study conducted on time to recovery and its predictors among pediatric patients with severe community-acquired pneumonia admitted to public general hospitals of Tigray. A prospective follow-up study was conducted among 305 children using consecutive sampling to select the study participants from December 20, 2024, to February 20, 2025. The collected data were entered into Epi-Data version 4.7 and then exported to STATA version 14 for further statistical analysis. The Kaplan-Meier curve was used to estimate recovery time. Both bivariable and multivariable Cox regression models were applied to analyze the data. Finally, the results were reported with 95% confidence intervals, and variables with a p-value < 0.05 were considered statistically significant. The recovery rate among pediatric patients was 85.2%, with a median recovery time of 5 days. The overall incidence of recovery rate was 16.30 per 100 person days observation (95% CI: 14.43-18.40). Being rural residence (AHR = 0.69;95%CI (0.53-0.90), late presenter to seeking care (AHR = 0.56; 95% CI (0.35-0.88), absence of danger sign (AHR = 1.48; 95% CI: 1.07-2.05)), absence of comorbidity (AHR = 3.02; 95% CI: 2.15-4.22) and not receiving oxygen therapy (AHR = 1.71; 95% CI: 1.20-2.41), were significant predictors. The median recovery time of patients was considerably high. Rural residence, late presentation for care, absence of danger signs, absence of comorbidity, and not receiving oxygen therapy were statistically significant predictors of recovery time.

title: Efficacy, Safety, and Economic Evaluation of Originator Versus Generic Moxifloxacin Hydrochloride Injection in the Treatment of Community-Acquired Pneumonia Under China's National Centralized Drug Procurement Policy: A Retrospective Study.
text: To investigate the efficacy, safety and economic outcomes of moxifloxacin hydrochloride injection in the treatment of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) under the centralized volume-based procurement policy, and to provide a basis for its rational clinical application. Inpatients with CAP who received moxifloxacin hydrochloride injection as initial therapy across 4 tertiary hospitals from January 2019 to March 2024 were retrospectively enrolled and divided into the originator group (Group A) and the NCDP-selected generic group (Group B) based on the drug source. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was applied to balance baseline confounding factors. Efficacy was evaluated by comparing primary and secondary outcomes such as the clinical efficacy and microbial clearance rates; for missing data regarding efficacy outcomes, complete-case analysis and baseline observation carried forward (BOCF) were adopted for sensitivity testing. Concurrently, exploratory subgroup analyses based on different treatment regimens and the concurrent-use period were conducted to evaluate the stability of moxifloxacin's efficacy and control for potential temporal confounding. Safety was assessed based on the incidence of total and specific adverse reactions. Economic evaluation utilized a cost-consequences analysis (CCA), and the robustness of the conclusions was assessed through sensitivity analyses (including a generalized linear model and bootstrap resampling). Group A and Group B included 414 and 455 patients, respectively. After balancing via IPTW, there were no statistical differences in baseline characteristics between the 2 groups. In terms of efficacy, there were no statistical differences between the 2 groups in the primary and secondary outcomes (P > 0.05). The sensitivity analysis for missing data supported the robustness of the main analysis results. Furthermore, exploratory subgroup analyses showed no statistical differences in efficacy among the treatment regimen subgroups, suggesting that the effect of moxifloxacin is relatively stable. Additionally, the subgroup analysis based on the concurrent-use period indicated that the comparative effectiveness was not significantly affected by calendar time. In terms of safety, no statistically significant differences were observed in the incidence of total and specific adverse reactions between the 2 groups (P > 0.05). Economically, with no statistically significant difference observed clinically, the base-case CCA and sensitivity analyses showed significantly lower average total medical costs in the NCDP-selected group. Under the centralized procurement policy, the NCDP-selected generic moxifloxacin showed clinical efficacy and safety not significantly different from those of the originator, while being associated with lower total medical costs. These findings require further validation in large‑sample studies.

title: Decreasing Ambulatory Antibiotic Treatment Duration for Acute Otitis Media and Community-Acquired Pneumonia.
text: Despite evidence supporting short treatment duration for acute otitis media and community-acquired pneumonia, many patients receive longer courses. The aim was to increase the proportion of short-duration antibiotic therapy from 40% to 80% within 9 months in primary care, emergency department, and urgent care settings spanning 3 states. This quality improvement initiative was conducted from June 2022 to March 2025. Interventions were implemented through 7 plan-do-study-act cycles, including creation of a clinical pathway and electronic health record tools with subsequent enhancements, education, organizational support via physician incentivization and alignment with organizational goals, data sharing, gemba walks, and positive reinforcement. Change in the outcome (percentage of encounters receiving short-duration therapy and the mean duration of therapy), process (percentage of encounters utilizing order panels) and balancing (treatment failure) measures over time were analyzed using statistical process control charts. About 51,056 patients were included, with 18,040 patients in the baseline and 33,016 in the implementation phase. Short-duration antibiotic therapy increased from 40% to 88% and improved across all race, ethnicity, and child opportunity indices (P<.001). Minimal baseline disparities were further attenuated. Mean antibiotic duration decreased from 8 to 5.9 days, saving 42,141 cumulative antibiotic days. Treatment failure remained unchanged (5%, range 2.5%-7.8%). Quality improvement methodology led to system-wide decrease in antibiotic duration across demographics in 2 common pediatric diagnoses. Aligning with organizational goals and data sharing proved to be effective strategies to promote large-scale practice change. N/A.

title: Monozygotic Twins with biallelic TSHR Mutations and discordance for Congenital Hypothyroidism.
text: Congenital hypothyroidism (CH) occurs due to abnormal thyroid development or impaired hormone synthesis in a normally sited gland. Its pathogenesis is ill-defined, and although mutations in thyroidal genes, e.g. thyroid stimulating hormone receptor (TSHR), may be implicated, discordance in monozygotic twins is common, suggesting involvement of non-Mendelian mechanisms. Here, a monozygotic twin was diagnosed with CH (TSH > 150mU/L (NR 0.35-5.5), free T4 3pmol/L (NR 9-23)) and thyroid hypoplasia associated with compound heterozygous mutations in TSHR. His twin brother was euthyroid at birth with normal thyroid morphology, despite harbouring the same TSHR mutations which have previously been associated with CH. We conclude that the impact of TSHR mutations on thyroid gland development and function is highly variable, even in individuals with near-identical germline genomes. This case report highlights the complexity of CH aetiology, potentially involving hitherto unidentified non-Mendelian genetic, epigenetic or environmental mechanisms in addition to a germline predisposition.

title: Severe Hypothyroidism Causing Reversible Pacing Failure: A Case Report and Literature Review.
text: Pacemakers are implantable electronic devices used in patients with conduction disorders to deliver electrical stimuli, configured with predetermined settings. These devices facilitate effective myocyte contraction and maintain the heart's electrical excitability. Pacemaker malfunctions can arise from sensing or pacing issues and manifest in various clinical presentations. Although malfunctions often involve anomalies in the pulse generator or leads, underlying conditions and diseases affecting the conduction system may be principal causes; thus, their management can lead to rectification of the malfunction. We present a case of a 66-year-old woman with asymptomatic profound hypothyroidism revealed through pacemaker malfunction, with restoration of normal pacemaker function following thyroid hormone replacement.

title: Anxiogenic- and depressant-like behaviors in parents and offspring due to parents' hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism in mice.
text: Thyroid hormone dysfunctions have long been related to mood disorders, but the causal relationship between parents' thyroid dysfunctions and mood disorders of parents and offspring remains controversial. To find this question, we administrated mice models of hyperthyroidism using L-thyroxin and hypothyroidism using lithium carbonate as well as using the three-chamber paradigm test, the elevated-plus maze (EPM) test, forced swimming test (FST), and tail suspension test (TST) for assessment of social, anxiety, and depression behaviors. The results of this research exhibited that treatment with L-thyroxin and lithium carbonate in parents had no significant effect on social motivation and novelty of parents and offspring in the three-chamber paradigm test (P > 0.05). Furthermore, induction of hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism in parents caused anxiogenic-like behavior in parents and offspring via reduction of %OAT (P < 0.001) and %OAE (P < 0.01) but not locomotor activity (P > 0.05). Also, administration of L-thyroxin and lithium carbonate in parents induced depressant-like response in parents and offspring due to the enhancement of immobility time in the FST (P < 0.05) and TST (P < 0.05). In conclusion, these findings suggested that induction of hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism in parents induced anxiogenic- and depressant-like behaviors in parents and offspring.

title: Barbed Dissolving Poly-γ-Glutamic Acid Microneedles for Reduced-Frequency Transdermal Levothyroxine Delivery in Hypothyroidism.
text: Hypothyroidism often requires lifelong thyroid hormone replacement, but oral levothyroxine (LT4) treatment depends on daily administration and gastrointestinal absorption. Here, we developed an LT4-loaded barbed dissolving microneedle patch based on poly-γ-glutamic acid (γ-PGA) (LT4@MN) for reduced-frequency transdermal delivery. LT4 was incorporated into the needle region, while the γ-PGA backing was prepared without the drug. The microneedles exhibited well-defined morphology, sufficient mechanical strength, moisture-responsive dissolution behavior, effective skin penetration to a depth of approximately 700 μm, and favorable cytocompatibility. In a total thyroidectomy-induced hypothyroid rat model, LT4@MN administered once every 6 days increased serum total thyroxine (TT4) from the hypothyroid baseline and maintained elevated TT4 levels across three consecutive treatment cycles. However, serum thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) did not show a clear sustained decrease during treatment. Repeated application caused no obvious local tissue damage or histopathological abnormalities in major organs. These findings support the feasibility of reduced-frequency transdermal LT4 delivery using barbed dissolving γ-PGA microneedles and highlight their potential as a minimally invasive alternative to daily oral administration.

title: Difficult Extubation After Thoracoscopic Surgery in a Patient With Hypothyroidism: A Case Report.
text: BACKGROUND Hypothyroidism is a common endocrine disorder with a prevalence of 0.4% to 1.7%, affecting predominantly women and older adults. Common anesthetic and surgical complications in patients with hypothyroidism include delayed emergence, myocardial and pulmonary infarction, respiratory arrest, hemorrhage, and fluid or electrolyte imbalance. Severe hypothyroidism can rarely trigger myxedema. This case report describes the case of a patient with hypothyroidism who underwent difficult extubation after thoracoscopic lung surgery. CASE REPORT A 62-year-old woman with hypothyroidism developed shortness of breath, stridor, hypoxemia, and decreased muscle strength in the extremities following the removal of a double-lumen endotracheal tube after thoracoscopic resection of the right lung S6 segment. Reintubation revealed marked periglottic edema. Upon admission to the intensive care unit, she presented with lethargy, cold extremities, and edema of the eyelids and dorsum of the feet. A detailed medical history revealed irregular use of levothyroxine sodium and self-discontinuation of the medication for 3 days prior to surgery. Postoperative laryngeal edema was considered the direct cause of extubation difficulty, while inadequately controlled hypothyroidism was identified as a major contributing factor to tissue edema, impaired respiratory muscle function, and delayed postoperative recovery. Following respiratory support and supplementation with levothyroxine sodium, respiratory function and muscle strength gradually improved, and the patient was discharged on the sixth postoperative day. CONCLUSIONS This case suggests that in patients with hypothyroidism experiencing difficulty with extubation during the perioperative period, a comprehensive assessment of common causes, such as airway edema and residual neuromuscular blockade, is necessary, and the adverse effects of hypothyroidism on airway edema and recovery from anesthesia should be given due attention.
source: The American journal of case reports

title: Quality-recommendation paradox in adult hypothyroidism guidelines: a systematic appraisal of methodological quality, recommendation consistency, and citation impact.
text: Hypothyroidism is one of the most common endocrine disorders, yet its adult guidelines disagree on screening, on treatment thresholds for subclinical disease, and on combination therapy. Whether higher methodological quality yields more conservative, more actionable, or more influential guidance remains unclear. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, CNKI, and VIP were searched from January 1, 2010 to August 25, 2026. Eligible documents were clinical practice guidelines and standard documents for adult hypothyroidism, published in Chinese or English. Four raters assessed all included documents with the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation II (AGREE II) instrument. Domain scores, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs), recommendation consistency, version evolution, emerging-topic coverage, and citation impact were examined. The study was registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; CRD420261487294). Fifteen guidelines were included: 12 English and 3 Chinese documents (2012-2025). Eight of 15 reached an overall quality score of at least 5.5 and were recommended for use. BMJ 2019 (6.25), AACE/ATA 2012 (6.20), and ETA 2025 (6.10) scored highest, and the two Chinese primary care guidelines scored lowest (4.86 and 4.77). For the thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) 4-10 mIU/L gray zone, BMJ 2019 avoided routine treatment, whereas ETA 2013 (5.76) was more interventional. Version evolution was evidence-driven in the ETA series but simplification-driven in Chinese primary care documents, and coverage of artificial intelligence, laboratory standardization, and reference intervals was largely descriptive. Exploratory analysis showed only weak quality-citation correlation (Spearman rho = 0.368, n = 13). Average ICC(2,k) values ranged from 0.651 to 0.895 across domains. Mean overall quality ranged from 4.77 to 6.25, and only 8 of 15 (53%) earned an unqualified recommendation for use; the most rigorous documents were BMJ Rapid Recommendations, AACE/ATA 2012, and ETA 2025. Rigorous guidelines often acknowledge uncertainty, whereas less rigorous documents supply clearer directives. In gray-zone decisions such as TSH 4-10 mIU/L, clinicians should pair guideline appraisal with explicit evidence summaries and should not assume that the most decisive advice is the most reliable. Guideline developers should strengthen stakeholder involvement, applicability, and scheduled updating.

title: Bridging Evidence and Practice: Recent Advances in Hypothyroidism Management during Pregnancy.
text: Deficiency of thyroid hormones, primarily thyroxine and triiodothyronine, results in the clinical condition known as hypothyroidism, a prevalent endocrine disorder globally, particularly in women of childbearing age. Dynamic changes occur in thyroid function during pregnancy to provide adequate levels of thyroid hormones to the mother and the fetus. Hashimoto thyroiditis remains the most widespread reason for gestational hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient regions and in mildly iodine deficient populations. Iodine plays a vital role in the synthesis and regulation of thyroid hormones; therefore, during pregnancy, iodine consumption must be increased by 50% to produce the required amount of maternal thyroid hormones and meet the increased demand of the developing fetus. Evidence-based studies have shown that even minor alteration in maternal thyroid function can cause pregnancy-related complications and adverse pregnancy outcomes (e.g. miscarriage, perinatal death, pre-eclampsia, pregnancy-induced hypertension, low birth weight and postpartum hemorrhage). Therefore, the timely assessment and appropriate management of gestational hypothyroidism is crucial to ensure optimal maternal and fetal outcomes. Levothyroxine remains the standard treatment for hypothyroidism, significantly reducing the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes in women with hypothyroidism. The present review provides an update on the diagnosis and management of hypothyroidism in pregnant women, highlighting the different types, causes, signs and symptoms of hypothyroidism, and the obstetric outcomes of each type of hypothyroidism along with the treatment strategy. Current key recommendations based on clinical evidence by health practitioners are also provided to assist in planning and choosing the individualized treatment regimen for patients with hypothyroidism before and during pregnancy.
source: Hormone and metabolic research = Hormon- und Stoffwechselforschung = Hormones et metabolisme

title: Hypothyroidism Improves Survival in Experimental Peritonitis.
text: Hypothyroidism decreases the basal metabolic rate. Using three models of peritonitis, intraperitoneal LPS plus Zymosan challenge, cecal slurry-induced intraperitoneal infection, and cecal ligation and puncture, we demonstrate that hypothyroid mice show enhanced survival compared to euthyroid mice. Hypothyroid mice show lower energy expenditure, reduced CO2/O2 exchange, and decreased movements prior to treatment. However, they maintain greater physiological stability following LPS plus zymosan challenge and are capable of recovering homeostatic values. In contrast, euthyroid mice, which begin with higher energy expenditure and CO2/O2 exchange rates, show a rapid sharp decline and severe hypoglycemia after treatment, not observed in hypothyroid mice. Two days postchallenge, hypothyroid mice exhibit decreased levels of circulating proinflammatory cytokines and tissue-specific IL-6 in liver, lung, and kidney. Consequently, hypothyroid mice exhibit significantly lower circulating levels of systemic, hepatic, renal, and pulmonary tissue-damage markers. These findings correlate with a decrease in ferroptosis and an attenuation of hepatic phospholipid peroxidation. In the early hours following peritoneal cecal slurry-induced infection, hypothyroid mice display a significant decrease in peritoneal levels of proinflammatory cytokines and circulating neutrophil counts. Crucially, both groups show comparable intraperitoneal bacterial proliferation, similar counts of both large and small peritoneal macrophages, with an analogous phagocytic capacity and similar disappearance rate. In conclusion, hypothyroidism increases tolerance to polymicrobial peritoneal infection, specifically by mitigating inflammation and disease severity while leaving bacterial dynamics unaffected.

title: Well-controlled hypothyroidism does not affect the macronutrient composition of colostrum.
text: Maternal hypothyroidism is a common endocrine disorder occurring during pregnancy and has been associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. When untreated or poorly controlled, hypothyroidism may influence lactation and milk composition, although the effects of well-controlled hypothyroidism on human milk remain insufficiently characterised. This prospective cohort study included 120 postpartum women: 45 with well-controlled hypothyroidism treated with levothyroxine during pregnancy and 75 healthy controls. We collected colostrum samples within the first 5 days postpartum and analysed them using mid-infrared spectroscopy (MIRIS®) to determine macronutrient composition, including lipids, protein, carbohydrates, total solids, and energy content. We used the Mann-Whitney test for statistical analysis, with effect size assessed by Cliff's delta. No a priori power analysis was conducted; therefore, interpret the results in light of the sample size and observed effect sizes. No significant differences were observed between the hypothyroid and control groups in any measured component of milk composition, including lipids, crude and true protein, carbohydrates, total solids, or energy content (for all components, the p value > 0.05). Effect sizes were negligible across all variables. Additionally, there was no significant difference in neonatal outcomes and maternal characteristics between groups, indicating appropriate clinical management of hypothyroidism during pregnancy. Well-controlled maternal hypothyroidism treated during pregnancy does not affect the macronutrient composition or energy content of colostrum in early lactation. The results indicate that adequate treatment of hypothyroidism does not affect the macronutrient composition or energy content of early colostrum. However, additional research to assess the composition of mature milk, the bio-active components and long term lactational outcomes must be done before wider implications for breastfeeding and human milk donation can be made.

title: Pulp response to cold and electrical sensibility tests in patients with hypothyroidism: an analytical cross-sectional study.
text: Thyroid disorders are the second most common endocrine diseases worldwide. Hypothyroidism has been associated with peripheral neuropathy; however, its potential effects on dental pulp sensibility remain poorly understood. This study aimed to compare responses to cold and electric pulp tests (EPT) between patients with hypothyroidism and healthy individuals. This analytical cross-sectional study was conducted at the Endocrinology Clinic of Shahid Sadoughi Hospital, Yazd, Iran. A total of 292 participants aged 18-58 years were enrolled, including 146 patients with primary hypothyroidism and 146 age-matched healthy participants. The study population was predominantly female (144 females and 2 males in the hypothyroid group; 138 females and 8 males in the healthy group). Primary hypothyroidism was confirmed by an endocrinologist based on elevated serum thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and reduced free thyroxine (T4) levels. One maxillary central incisor from each participant was evaluated using the cold test and EPT. The EPT threshold and response latency to the cold test were recorded. Data were analyzed using the independent t-test, with statistical significance set at P < 0.05. The mean EPT threshold was significantly lower in the hypothyroid group than in the healthy group (2.22 ± SD vs. 2.42 ± SD, P = 0.015; scale: 0-10). Likewise, the mean response latency to the cold test was significantly shorter in patients with hypothyroidism than in healthy participants (2.14 ± SD vs. 2.37 ± SD seconds, P = 0.023). Patients with hypothyroidism exhibited significantly lower electrical stimulation thresholds and shorter response latencies to cold stimuli than healthy individuals. These findings suggest altered dental pulp neural sensitivity in patients with hypothyroidism and support the potential influence of thyroid dysfunction on pulpal sensory responses.

title: Refractory hypothyroidism.
text: Refractory hypothyroidism is generally defined as persistent biochemical hypothyroidism despite levothyroxine (LT4) doses exceeding 1.9-2.5 μg/kg/day. Although malabsorption has traditionally been considered a major cause, accumulating evidence indicates that poor adherence, inappropriate administration, and drug or dietary interactions affecting LT4 bioavailability account for a substantial proportion of cases. Medical history, clinical context, and laboratory investigations can help to guide the diagnosis. When no cause is apparent, LT4 absorption test can distinguish true malabsorption from preserved absorption, most commonly reflecting poor adherence or other causes of pseudo-malabsorption. However, protocols vary considerably, and their diagnostic performances have not been rigorously established. This review summarizes the physiology of LT4 absorption, presents the main causes of refractory hypothyroidism, discusses the diagnosis work-up, with particular attention to the strengths and limitations of the LT4 absorption tests, and details the therapeutic approach for clinicians managing these challenging patients.
source: Best practice & research. Clinical endocrinology & metabolism

title: Biochemical Characteristics, Treatment, and Outcomes of Thyrotoxicosis in Amiodarone-Treated Individuals with Prior Hypothyroidism.
text: Evidence regarding the transition from hypothyroidism to thyrotoxicosis in amiodarone-treated patients remains scarce. We compared clinical characteristics, treatments, and outcomes of amiodarone-exposed individuals developing thyrotoxicosis following hypothyroidism (post-hypo-T) versus those without prior thyroid disease (T-controls). This retrospective cohort study utilized electronic health records from a large health maintenance organization (HMO). We included adults from the cardiovascular disease registry with new-onset thyrotoxicosis diagnosed between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2022, who received amiodarone within the year preceding diagnosis. Follow-up ended on August 31, 2025. Cox regression models adjusted for age and sex were used to analyze outcomes. Of 558 individuals, 91 (16%) had prior hypothyroidism and 467 were controls. Post-hypo-T patients were older (70.4±10.1 vs. 67.4±11.0 years; p = 0.02) and had a higher proportion of males (44.0% vs. 25.3%; p < 0.001). Median amiodarone exposure prior to diagnosis was 2.7 versus 2.8 years, respectively (p = 0.01). At diagnosis, post-hypo-T individuals had lower median free thyroxine (fT4) levels (27.0 vs. 31.3 pmol/L; p < 0.001) and free triiodothyronine (fT3) levels (6.4 vs. 7.5 pmol/L; p < 0.001).Over a 7.8-year median follow-up, antithyroid medications were used less frequently in post-hypo-T individuals (37.4% vs. 54.0%; p = 0.004). Glucocorticoid use was numerically lower in post-hypo-T individuals (26.4% vs. 38.5%; p = 0.06). Post-hypo-T individuals had a higher incidence of hypothyroidism requiring levothyroxine (64.8% vs. 17.8%; p < 0.001). Among amiodarone-exposed individuals who develop thyrotoxicosis, those with prior hypothyroidism have a milder biochemical presentation, less frequent use of antithyroid drugs or glucocorticoids, and a higher likelihood of recurrent hypothyroidism requiring levothyroxine.

title: Severe Iodine Deficiency-Associated Hypothyroidism in a Toddler With Cow's Milk Allergy: A Case Report.
text: Iodine is an essential micronutrient required for thyroid hormone synthesis and normal growth and neurodevelopment. Although iodine deficiency is uncommon in high-income countries with iodization programs, children with restrictive diets may remain at risk. We report a 23-month-old male who presented with growth deceleration and was found to have severe hypothyroidism. Initial laboratory evaluation demonstrated low FT4 with markedly elevated thyroid-stimulating hormone (> 200 mIU/L). Endocrine evaluation revealed diffuse thyroid enlargement with hypervascularity on ultrasonography and elevated thyroglobulin levels, with negative thyroid autoantibodies. Urinary iodine-to-creatinine ratio was low, consistent with iodine deficiency. Dietary review revealed multiple immunoglobulin E-mediated food allergies, including cow's milk allergy, and reliance on commercially available allergy-free foods lacking iodized salt. The patient was treated with levothyroxine, resulting in rapid normalization of thyroid function. Follow-up demonstrated improvement in urinary iodine levels and resolution of thyroid enlargement. This case highlights iodine deficiency as a reversible cause of severe hypothyroidism and growth delay in young children with restrictive diets. Clinicians should consider iodine deficiency in toddlers with food allergies and growth abnormalities, even in regions where iodine sufficiency is presumed.

title: Serum FT3/FT4 ratio may indicate the degree of T3 compensation in congenital hypothyroidism.
text: Clinical guidelines for hypothyroidism recommend measuring serum thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and free thyroxine (FT4) levels as diagnostic and treatment efficacy indicators. However, they do not recommend measuring serum free triiodothyronine (FT3) levels because serum FT3 levels often remain within the normal range. However, serum TSH and FT4 levels alone make diagnosis and treatment decision-making difficult in conditions such as central hypothyroidism, suggesting the need for an additional indicator distinct from serum TSH levels. We investigated whether the serum FT3/FT4 ratio could be an indicator of congenital hypothyroidism (CH) severity, instead of serum TSH level. Thirty-seven newborns were diagnosed with CH (severe group (n = 13): serum TSH ≥ 30 mIU/L; moderate group (n = 24): serum TSH ≥ 5 to < 30 mIU/L). All infants in the severe group received thyroid hormone (TH) replacement therapy vs 13 infants in the moderate group (moderate group with CH). Serum TSH, FT4, FT3, and FT3/FT4 ratios were compared between each group and the two control groups of different ages at diagnosis and 2 months after treatment. The serum FT3/FT4 ratio was elevated before treatment compared with the control group, reflecting CH severity. Two months after TH replacement, the serum FT3/FT4 ratio decreased significantly: severe group: at diagnosis, 0.48 vs 2 months, 0.27, p =<0.0001; moderate group with TH: 0.38 vs 2 months, 0.26, p < 0.0001. No change was observed in infants without TH replacement. A high serum FT3/FT4 ratio in CH could reflect the degree of systemic T3 compensation and is an indicator of CH severity. This ratio may also be applicable in conditions in which serum TSH levels are not useful for diagnosis or when assessing treatment outcomes. A high serum FT3/FT4 ratio may be an indicator of hypothyroidism severity.

title: Claims-defined adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism, and type 1 diabetes after immune checkpoint inhibitor initiation in patients with triple-negative breast cancer in Japan.
text: The incidence of treated adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism, and type 1 diabetes after immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) treatment for triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) has not been fully characterized in real-world clinical practice in Japan. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the JMDC claims database, which includes employees of Japanese companies and their dependents. Patients aged 18-74 years with TNBC who received atezolizumab or pembrolizumab between January 2005 and June 2025 were included. Early-stage and advanced TNBC were identified based on the treatment regimen at ICI initiation. We examined the incidence rates and time to onset of claims-defined adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism, and type 1 diabetes separately in the two cohorts. The study included 569 patients with early-stage TNBC (median age, 50.8 years) and 254 with advanced TNBC (median age, 52.8 years). In early-stage TNBC, the incidence rates (95% CIs) of adrenal insufficiency and hypothyroidism were 5.6 (4.0-7.8) and 12.7 (10.0-16.0) cases/100 person-years (PY), respectively. The median times to onset (IQRs) were 124 (86-215) and 117 (89-196) days, respectively. In advanced TNBC, the incidence rates (95% CIs) of adrenal insufficiency and hypothyroidism were 1.4 (0.53-3.8) and 9.2 (6.1-13.8) cases/100 PY, respectively. The median time to onset of hypothyroidism was 84 (63-105) days. Type 1 diabetes was rare. This study provides real-world estimates of claims-defined endocrine outcomes after ICI initiation separately in patients with early-stage and advanced TNBC in Japan.

title: Extreme Bradycardia in Brash Syndrome Unmasked by Severe Amiodarone-Induced Hypothyroidism.
text: BRASH syndrome - bradycardia, renal failure, AV nodal blockade, shock and hyperkalaemia - is a self-amplifying pathophysiological loop. Its association with severe amiodarone-induced hypothyroidism is rarely described in detail. A 79-year-old woman with permanent atrial fibrillation on long-term amiodarone and bisoprolol presented after prolonged unwitnessed floor immobilisation with extreme bradycardia (24-30 bpm), haemodynamic instability, KDIGO stage 3 acute kidney injury, hyperkalaemia (5.5 mmol/l), metabolic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis and profound hypothyroidism (TSH 68.5 mUI/l; free T4 4.62 pmol/l) against a normal thyroid baseline 13 months prior. The Popoveniuc myxoedema coma score was 45 (high-risk zone). High-sensitivity troponin T showed flat kinetics consistent with type 2 myocardial injury. Isoproterenol was required for bradycardia refractory to initial metabolic correction, achieving a ventricular rate of 62-68 bpm with QTc shortening from 0.62 s to 0.38 s. The patient was discharged on day 8 with renal recovery and improving thyroid function. Thyroid antibody negativity at 30-day follow-up was consistent with an amiodarone-induced rather than autoimmune aetiology. This case illustrates BRASH syndrome presenting with only mild hyperkalaemia in the context of severe amiodarone-induced hypothyroidism, which may have potentiated the pathophysiological loop. Systematic thyroid monitoring during long-term amiodarone therapy and multi-target metabolic correction, including isoproterenol as a pharmacological bridge, may avert invasive pacing. BRASH syndrome may occur with only mild hyperkalaemia when severe hypothyroidism potentiates AV nodal blockade - disproportionate bradycardia relative to potassium level is the key diagnostic signal.In any patient on long-term amiodarone presenting with otherwise unexplained bradycardia, profound hypothyroidism should be actively excluded before attributing the presentation to drug toxicity alone; thyroid function testing every 3-6 months is guideline-recommended during such therapy.Isoproterenol may serve as an effective pharmacological chronotropic bridge in BRASH syndrome refractory to initial metabolic correction, potentially avoiding invasive temporary pacing.
source: European journal of case reports in internal medicine

title: Case Report: Hyperactive delirium with psychotic symptoms associated with severe hypothyroidism during pembrolizumab therapy. Complete remission after levothyroxine and no recurrence after pembrolizumab rechallenge.
text: Thyroid dysfunction is a common adverse event during pembrolizumab therapy, but severe hypothyroidism accompanied by acute neuropsychiatric symptoms is rare. We present the case of a 78-year-old woman with metastatic colorectal cancer who developed agitation, hallucinations, and confusion three months after initiation of Pembrolizumab. Evaluation revealed profound hypothyroidism (TSH 37.9 mU/L, free T3 <0.60 pmol/L and free T4 <0.5 pmol/L) and moderate hyponatremia without acute findings on neuroimaging. Levothyroxine therapy led to complete remission of neuropsychiatric symptoms, and pembrolizumab was safely restarted with close monitoring and no recurrence. This case underscores the importance of assessing thyroid function in acute psychiatric presentations during immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy and supports cautious rechallenge after stabilization. Severe hypothyroidism was considered a major contributor, although a multifactorial delirium, including the contribution of hyponatremia and the absence of CSF/EEG evaluation, cannot be excluded.

title: Herpes zoster-induced critical rhabdomyolysis with secondary hypothyroidism: a case report.
text: Primary varicella-zoster virus (VZV) reactivation causes herpes zoster (HZ), typically presenting with dermatomal rash and neuropathic pain. Rhabdomyolysis as a systemic complication of HZ is extremely rare, and its underlying pathogenesis and optimal management remain poorly characterized, especially in elderly patients. Here we report a 63-year-old female who presented with fever, generalized myalgia, and oliguria, with serum creatine kinase (CK) rapidly escalating from 4,383 U/L to a peak of 186,383 U/L. Further investigation revealed a preceding history of lumbar herpes zoster two weeks prior, accompanied by virus-induced secondary hypothyroidism. Muscle biopsy confirmed extensive myofiber necrosis without inflammatory infiltration, consistent with non-inflammatory rhabdomyolysis. The patient developed acute kidney injury, hepatic dysfunction, and respiratory failure, and was managed with multidisciplinary intensive care including mechanical ventilation, 9 days of continuous renal replacement therapy, glucocorticoid anti-inflammatory therapy, and levothyroxine replacement. After 12 days of treatment, CK decreased to 3,381 U/L with significant recovery of multiorgan function, and the patient was transferred out of the intensive care unit. This case highlights that HZ can trigger life-threatening rhabdomyolysis, possibly via VZV-mediated immune dysregulation and secondary hypothyroidism. Detailed history taking, early CK screening, and multidisciplinary organ support are critical to improve outcomes in this rare but severe condition.

title: Re-evaluating the Concept of Peripheral Hypothyroidism.
text: Isolated peripheral hypothyroidism comprises a group of disorders in which cellular thyroid hormone action is impaired because of defects in membrane transport or intracellular metabolism, despite normal or increased thyroid hormone secretion. Because serum T4, T3, and TSH concentrations often remain within the normal range and sensitive markers of tissue thyroid status are lacking, diagnosis remains challenging. This review examines the causes of isolated peripheral hypothyroidism and recent advances in its management. A MEDLINE search covering 2010 - 2025 was conducted using the terms peripheral hypothyroidism, tissue-specific hypothyroidism, and cellular hypothyroidism, supplemented by manual screening of reference lists. After abstract screening, full-text articles were assessed for eligibility, duplicates were removed, and only studies with appropriate designs were included. The causes can be categorized into four groups: 1) decreased peripheral T3 availability, as observed in patients receiving levothyroxine (LT4) monotherapy who have persistent symptoms associated with low serum T3:T4 ratios despite normal serum T4, T3, and TSH concentrations; 2) peripheral cellular dysfunction, reported in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), skeletal muscle changes during weight regain, and organ-specific conditions involving the heart, lungs, and kidneys, suggesting widespread tissue involvement; 3) altered deiodinase activity, including shifts toward reverse T3 production during cellular dysfunction and consumptive hypothyroidism caused by marked DIO3 overexpression in tumors such as hemangiomas; and 4) thyroid hormone receptor alterations, such as thyroid hormone receptor mutations causing resistance. Isolated peripheral hypothyroidism comprises a diverse and often underrecognized group of disorders because standard biochemical tests may appear normal. Promising therapies include thyroid hormone combinations, such as levothyroxine plus slow-release T3, and thyromimetics, such as resmetirom for MASLD. This review synthesizes recent findings on cellular hypothyroidism, diagnostic challenges, and emerging multidisciplinary management strategies. Improved biomarkers and multidisciplinary evaluation are still needed to advance its diagnosis and management.
source: International journal of endocrinology and metabolism

title: Early thyroid-stimulating hormone dynamics as an independent predictor of immune-related hypothyroidism during nivolumab therapy.
text: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment landscape of advanced solid tumors, yet immune-related adverse events remain a major challenge. Thyroid dysfunction is among the most frequent endocrine toxicities associated with programmed cell death-1 (PD-1) inhibitors, often evolving dynamically and remaining early immune-mediated thyroid injury. Identifying an early and reliable biomarker for immune-related hypothyroidism could improve patient monitoring and treatment safety. This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 214 adult patients with solid tumors treated with nivolumab between January 2020 and January 2025. Thyroid function tests obtained at baseline and at the first month of treatment were analyzed. Early thyroid-stimulating hormone change (ΔTSH) was defined as change from baseline, calculated as first-month TSH minus baseline TSH. The primary endpoint was the development of de-novo or deteriorated hypothyroidism. Time-to-event analyses were performed using Cox proportional hazards regression. The discriminative performance of ΔTSH was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, with internal validation using 2,000 bootstrap resamples. During follow-up, nivolumab-related thyroid adverse events occurred in 37 patients (17.3%), with de novo or deteriorated hypothyroidism observed in 27 patients. Median time to hypothyroidism was 12 weeks (IQR: 8-24). In multivariable Cox regression, ΔTSH remained independently associated with subsequent hypothyroidism (adjusted HR per 1 mU/L increase: 1.060; 95% CI: 1.036-1.085; p < 0.001), together with age. Exploratory ROC analysis demonstrated high apparent discrimination of ΔTSH for subsequent hypothyroidism (AUC 0.952, 95% CI 0.925-0.979). Internal validation using 2,000 bootstrap resamples showed a mean AUC of 0.952 (95% bootstrap CI: 0.922-0.976). Early ΔTSH was associated with subsequent immune-related hypothyroidism in this retrospective cohort. However, the modest sample size of 214 patients and the limited number of hypothyroidism events (n = 27) mean that the observed association and apparent discriminative performance should be regarded as preliminary, exploratory evidence. Bootstrap resampling does not overcome these data limitations. Larger cohorts with more outcome events are needed to confirm predictive performance before clinical application. Not applicable.

title: Levothyroxine for subclinical hypothyroidism.
text: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (intervention). The objectives are as follows: To evaluate the benefits and harms of levothyroxine for adults with subclinical hypothyroidism, compared with placebo or no treatment.
source: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

title: Antithrombotic therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation and acute coronary syndrome treated with percutaneous coronary intervention. -insights from the SWEDEHEART registry.
text: The aim of this study was to study temporal changes in antithrombotic therapy and to assess associations between common treatment strategies and clinical outcomes. Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and acute coronary syndrome (ACS) undergoing PCI between 2010 and 2022 were identified from the SWEDEHEART registry. The three most common antithrombotic treatment strategies were: 1. Vitamin K antagonist (VKA)-based, 2. Direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC)-based, and 3. Platelet inhibition (PI) only. Outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; all-cause death, myocardial infarction (MI), or stroke), and net adverse cardiovascular event (NACE; MACE or major bleeding). Cox regression models were created to adjust for differences in baseline characteristics. In total, 15,358 patients were included, 29% were women and median age was 76 years. At discharge, 4155 (27%) received VKA-based, 4962 (32%) DOAC-based therapy, and 6241 (41%) PI only. The proportion treated with oral anticoagulants increased from 27% in 2010 to 82% in 2021. VKA-, and DOAC-based strategies were both associated with adjusted lower adjusted risk of MACE, (aHR 0.80, 95% CI 0.73-0.89) and (aHR 0.82, 95% CI 0.74-0.90) and NACE (aHR 0.86, 95% CI 0.78-0.94) and (aHR 0.85, 95% CI 0.77-0.93), respectively, compared with PI only, with no difference between the two OAC strategies. In patients with AF undergoing PCI for ACS, the use of oral anticoagulants increased over time. Both a VKA- and DOAC-based strategy were associated with lower MACE and NACE, with no significant difference between the two strategies.

title: Post-stroke atrial fibrillation detection with insertable cardiac monitors in older adults.
text: Older adults bear the greatest burden of atrial fibrillation (AF)-related stroke, yet national data on AF detection after insertable cardiac monitor (ICM) implantation following ischaemic stroke are limited. We evaluated the cumulative incidence of post-stroke AF detection and ICM monitoring intensity among Medicare beneficiaries receiving ICMs in routine clinical practice. This retrospective cohort study included Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries aged ≥66 years who underwent ICM implantation in 2017–2020 after ischaemic stroke, TIA or systemic thromboembolism without prior AF or oral anticoagulant (OAC) use. Outcomes were new AF and OAC-treated AF within 1 year, estimated using the Aalen-Johansen method with death as a competing risk. In a 90-day landmark cohort, we described monitoring intensity (interrogation encounters during days 1–90) and estimated associations between patient characteristics and subsequent AF detection using Poisson regression with and without monitoring intensity. Among 9284 beneficiaries (mean age 76.1 years; 54.0% women), the 1-year cumulative incidence of new AF was 24.4% (95% CI 23.5% to 25.3%), ranging from 21.6% to 27.6% across alternative AF definitions. AF detection was higher among individuals aged ≥75 versus 66–74 years (27.7% vs 20.7%). In the landmark cohort (n=8230), 14.3% had no interrogation encounter during days 1–90, with higher proportions among black (18.8%), Hispanic (22.3%), frail (16.3%) and dually eligible (21.8%) patients. Monitoring intensity was not associated with AF detection and did not explain lower detection among Black (incidence rate ratio (IRR), 0.64 (95% CI 0.49 to 0.83)), Hispanic (IRR, 0.71 (95% CI 0.51 to 1.00)) and frail (IRR, 0.86 (95% CI 0.77 to 0.97)) patients. Older adults undergoing ICM implantation after ischaemic stroke had a higher 1-year incidence of claims-based AF detection than reported in prior clinical trials. Monitoring intensity was lower among black, Hispanic, frail and dually eligible patients but did not explain the lower AF detection among black, Hispanic and frail patients.

title: Atrial Fibrillation Screening-to-Anticoagulation Pathways in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
text: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is an important cause of preventable stroke in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where diagnostic and treatment gaps may limit screening effectiveness. This study aims to evaluate AF screening in LMICs as a screening-to-anticoagulation pathway, focusing on reach, equity, diagnostic confirmation, anticoagulation uptake, and health-system capacity. MEDLINE via PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to July 2026. LMIC studies reporting population-facing AF screening or screening-linked care were included.
